## 10. Decisions for the owner

Each decision below changes what Bootwright promises, so the audit does not
take it. Each gives the options, what follows from each, and a
recommendation.

**1. What a stop code looks like.**
A readable name (`install.network-cutoff`) says what it is in the terminal
and continues today's dotted codes; its stability rests on discipline. A
number beside a class (`BW-6101`, class `lifecycle.effect-failed`) is short
to quote and lets the wording change, but means nothing without a lookup and
must never be reused. Recommendation: the readable name, with the cause and
the recovery as separate fields of the structured output.

**2. When a code becomes a promise.**
Frozen now: a renamed or removed code is a breaking change from the first
slice. Frozen at 1.0: until then the catalog test is the only rule, as for
every other format. Recommendation: at 1.0, in line with the development
policy.

**3. May text written by a task cross from the adapter to the operator.**
No: only names and closed tokens cross; the operator reads the rest with
`bootwright logs --raw`. The protocol's rule that no value crosses stays
whole. Yes, bounded: a failing task's own message (not under `no_log`, at
most about a thousand printable bytes) is shown and stored until its role is
converted; faster relief, but vendor text and interpolated values reach the
terminal, the structured output and the records. Recommendation: no. The
safety net of slice W1.4 (task name, step, host, kind) gives most of the
relief without it.

**4. A role failure that named no stop, after effects began: failed or
unknown.**
Failed, as today: the block is retried at once; a half-done effect is
converged by the retry. Unknown: the block is observed before anything else;
safer against a half-done effect, but it puts a resolution in front of every
such failure and blocks whenever the target cannot be observed, which is the
dead end of decision 5. Recommendation: keep failed, and let each role
declare, with a lint behind it, the steps that have no effect.

**5. A target that is gone for good.**
Today one unobservable block refuses the whole destroy, and the exit is to
delete the context and abandon everything it owns. Option A: keep that, and
make every such refusal name the deletion and list what it abandons.
Option B: add a scoped acknowledgement, in the manner of the erase
relaxation, by which the operator states that one host or one block is gone;
the removal records it as abandoned, with its inventory, and goes on with
the rest. B is narrower for the operator and is a new way past a refusal:
it needs a named safety slice. If B is taken, the reviewers' advice is that
the context must still be deleted with the orphan acknowledgement, so that
the evidence never reads as if nothing was abandoned. Recommendation: A now
(slice W1.5); decide B on its own, after A shows how often it is needed.

**6. A build update between a failed operation and its recovery.**
A fix that moves an execution contract makes the new build refuse to
continue or remove what the old build registered, and nothing keeps the old
build. Three independent options. (a) Keep the registering executable, by
digest, while an operation names it: every "use the build that registered
it" becomes a runnable command; costs disk and a supply-chain review.
(b) Let a destroy supersede an incomplete removal whose continuation the new
build cannot prove, resolving first, as it already does for an erase
relaxation: removes the largest dead end of the destroy flow without keeping
binaries. (c) Stop hashing Go type names into the fingerprint, so a pure
refactor no longer strands operations. Recommendation: (c) at once, as a
defect; (b) as a safety slice; (a) only if (b) and (c) leave cases behind.

**7. A destroy that pauses for Machines to stop.**
Today it prints a success headline, an error and exit status 1. Either it
is a pause the operator asked for (exit 0, as a paused apply) or a stop
that needs the operator (non-zero, with its own code and no success
headline). Recommendation: the second, because the operator must act before
the destroy can go on.

**8. An `explain` command, and who owns the catalog.**
`bootwright explain <code>` and `explain --context <name>` are new,
read-only commands. The catalog can be a spec table written by hand and held
equal to the code by a test, as the five transition tables are, or a page
generated from the Go declarations. Recommendation: the command, yes; the
table hand-written and tested, because specs own behavior here, with the
operator guide's reference generated from it.

**9. How far to take the machine.**
[Section 8.5](#85-how-far-to-take-the-machine): tables that decide and
tests that hold code and tables equal (depth 2), or an engine that runs from
the tables (depth 3). Recommendation: depth 2; revisit depth 3 if its checks
keep finding drift.

**10. Refusals before registration: remembered or recomputed.**
A destroy refused by the quiescence gate leaves no trace; `status` cannot
replay it because it cannot probe hosts. Logging the last refused invocation
as an event in the context's log area would let `status` show it. It is
troubleshooting material, not state. Recommendation: log it.

**11. Restore from a backup.**
Several remedies offer a restore of the context store or the keyring as the
first exit, and no command, procedure or test defines one (the parked item
on an explicit complete-store restore). Either define and test the
procedure, or stop offering it. Recommendation: stop offering it until the
procedure exists; name the exits that do exist.

**12. Parked items this plan would promote.**
The plan runs into work already recorded and parked: proving no guest uses a
network before its removal, the context incarnation in every ownership mark,
ending remote workers on cancellation, the store refusing transitions the
tables do not admit, pruning of finished operations, isolating a damaged
context, settling over restored input bytes, removing a failed addition
alone, online Ceph removal, and the reason in the attempt log.
[Appendix G](#appendix-g-already-recorded) lists them with their ids.
Promoting each is the owner's call; slices W5 and W6 say where each fits.

**13. Order.**
The plan puts the operator's view first (W1), then the codes (W2), then the
machine (W3, W4), because the first four slices answer the complaint that
started this audit and need no decision. The alternative is to build the
catalog first, so that every W1 change is written once in its final form;
it delays the relief by the size of W2.1. Recommendation: as planned; W1
writes its texts through a thin helper that W2.1 turns into declared stops.

## 11. Method, verification and limits

### 11.1 How the audit ran

The orchestrator froze the tree at `91f6e71b9` in a worktree of its own,
measured the baseline, wrote one brief for every reviewer, and ran the
audit in stages. Every agent was given its model and effort explicitly.

| Stage | Who | What |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Baseline | the orchestrator, with three small tools kept outside the repository | diagnostic emission sites and their messages and remedies in the Go code; failure constructs in the roles; outcomes in the retained private logs of 29 real runs |
| Review | 62 lanes, each one Claude Opus 5.5 agent at medium effort | 14 lanes on the engine, 17 on the capabilities and their roles and Python, 11 on the output, 18 cross-cutting (crash walks, dead ends, unprovable outcomes, concurrency, build updates, environment faults, waits, data safety, censoring, partial runs, tests, the two machine extractions, the two sets of operator journeys, preflight, bounds), and 2 added after a mechanical coverage check to read the files no lane had cited. Each returned its failure points, its findings with a quoted citation, and the implicit states it met |
| Census | 2 Claude Sonnet 5.5 agents at high effort | what the specs, the milestones, audits 003 and 005 and the knowledge pages already record in this area: 261 items, 13 candidates an earlier audit refuted, 24 earlier incidents |
| Duplicates | the orchestrator for the High findings, one Opus agent for the rest | 526 findings merged to 394 where one fix closes several; a pair was merged only as one defect with one root cause |
| Verification | 417 Sonnet votes and 53 Opus votes, 33 Opus arbitrations | every High and every Medium unsafe finding: a reproduce-and-contract lens (Sonnet, high effort) and a reachability-and-severity lens (Opus), with an Opus arbiter at high effort when they disagreed on the verdict. Every other Medium dead end or loose end: one Sonnet lens, and an Opus vote unless it simply confirmed. Other Medium findings: Sonnet, in batches of one lane, with an Opus vote on any refutation. Low findings: Sonnet, in batches of one lane |
| Reconcile | Sonnet, high effort | each record rewritten to state what the verifiers established, from the records and the verdicts only, without reading code |
| Source re-check | the orchestrator | four High findings read again at the source ([E05-01](#e05-01), [X04-01](#x04-01), [C10-01](#c10-01), [C07-01](#c07-01)); one severity raised against both verifiers, with the reason in its record ([E05-01](#e05-01)) |
| Design | 4 Opus designers, 3 Opus judges and 2 Opus drafters of the machine tables, at high effort | [section 8](#8-the-meta-view-the-flows-as-one-explicit-state-machine) and [Appendix E](#appendix-e-the-machine-as-implemented) |

Verification outcome: of 394 distinct findings, 14 were refuted, 104 were
confirmed as written and 276 were confirmed with a narrower scope or a
corrected detail. Of the 43 distinct findings reported as High, none was
refuted, 15 stayed High and 28 were lowered to Medium, mostly because the
cause they called unreachable can be read with `bootwright logs --raw`, or
because the dead end they describe is recorded policy with an existing,
unnamed exit; one of the 28 was raised back by the orchestrator. Severity
without an arbiter is the reachability lens's where that lens voted.

Citations were checked mechanically: for 519 of the 526 findings the quoted
text stands at a cited line of the frozen tree, for 6 it stands elsewhere in
the cited file, and for 1 it was not found; verifiers corrected lines where
they met them.

### 11.2 Limits

- **Nothing was run.** No agent ran a test, a build, a playbook or a
  Bootwright command. Every scenario was established by reading code; none
  was reproduced by execution.
- **Depth of verification follows severity.** A Medium output finding
  usually rests on its finder and one independent check, a Low finding on
  its finder and one batched check. The records show each finding's votes.
- **The map overlaps.** Lanes cover the flows from several sides on purpose,
  so the 1,247 failure-point families and the 497 implicit states contain
  repeats, and the counts of sites inside a family are the lanes' estimates.
  The percentages of section 2.6 describe the census, not unique code
  sites.
- **Coverage.** After the two added lanes, 91% of the 1,170 lifecycle
  emission sites sit in files a lane cited or read; the rest are mostly
  request and resource definition files of the Ceph capability.
- **The baseline tool is a heuristic.** It counts a site when a diagnostic
  code is the first argument of a call or the `Code` member of a literal,
  and classifies the message and the remedy from the argument text. Its
  totals are within one percent of a plain search for the code literals.
- **The real runs are the owner's virtual end-to-end runs.** No run on
  physical hardware is among them. Everything quoted from them is redacted.
- **The design was judged, not built.** Its feasibility claims were checked
  against the code by the judges; nothing was prototyped, and the sizes in
  the plan are estimates.
- **Main did not move** between the baseline and this report.

## Appendix A. Finding records

One record per verified finding, grouped by the lane that reported it. Each
record states what the verifiers established: where a finding was narrowed
or corrected, the record carries the corrected statement. The line under
the title gives the final severity, the kind, the flow and the votes. A
finding reported by several lanes appears once, under one id, and names the
others.

### Findings of lane C01

Libvirt provider host (Go capability, role and Python). Lane summary: [Lane
C01](#lane-c01).

#### C01-01

**An SSH provider host without virsh cannot be applied: the first host check
crashes on the missing program before the install task that would add
libvirt-client**

High · dead end · both · verified: combined confirmed, reach confirmed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/substrate_libvirt.py:802`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/bounded_process.py:94-95`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/modules/libvirt_host_inspect.py:62-63`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_libvirt_host/tasks/apply.yml:27`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_libvirt_host/tasks/apply.yml:42-53`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_libvirt_host/tasks/destroy.yml:27`

**Scenario:** A provider names a freshly installed RHEL Machine reached over
SSH. That install adds only the minimal environment plus the install profile's
packages, so it has no virsh. Nothing else adds libvirt-client: the host
prerequisites cover only the firewall. Apply runs the role. The first task
(apply.yml:27) calls observe_host, whose first step runs /usr/bin/virsh. The
runner raises FileNotFoundError for the missing program. observe_host has no
handler, and the module reports only the exception class name. The install
task at apply.yml:42, which would add libvirt-client, never runs, so every
repeat fails the same way. Destroy calls the same module and crashes the same
way if libvirt was removed by hand, instead of the designed 'hypervisor did
not answer' refusal (destroy.yml:45-50). The install path has never run live:
an earlier delivery record says the dnf step never ran. No shipped example
uses an SSH provider host; the journey is the spec's.

**What the operator sees:** Apply failed, a [FAIL] row for
substrate-host-\<provider>, 'the adapter operation did not complete'. In the
root-owned adapter output, the module's own text: 'the provider host could not
be observed: FileNotFoundError'.

**Impact:** The spec's SSH provider-host journey ('on an SSH host this block
installs the named packages') cannot work on a host without the libvirt
client, with no operator error involved. The message is an internal Python
token that names no command or package. The destroy variant is rare: it needs
libvirt removed by hand.

**Recovery today:** Install libvirt-client (or the whole package set) on the
host by hand, then repeat apply. Or, before the Machine is installed, list
libvirt-client in the install profile's spec.customizations.packages.install.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Make observe_host (uri_answers/invoke) treat a
missing program as 'did not answer' (uri false, hypervisor taken from the rpm
query), so the first observation succeeds and the install task runs. Add a
replay test with virsh absent.

#### C01-03

**policy trade-off: every host-block refusal shows as 'the adapter operation
did not complete' although the protocol has a refused phase that other roles
use**

Medium · output · both · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_libvirt_host/tasks/apply.yml:147-153`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/action/substrate_host_protocol.py:467-471`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/adapter_protocol.py:231-232`,
`internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/process_linux_amd64.go:510-511`,
`specs/substrates.md:386-389`, `specs/milestones/delivered.md:4224-4231`

**Scenario:** About 30 asserts across apply.yml and destroy.yml of the host
role guard against unsafe states: a foreign network of the same name, a route
collision, NetworkManager not ready, a Machine running on a drifted network, a
foreign pool, a missing bridge or MTU, firewalld not answering. When one
fires, the play fails and the runner maps the exit to 'the adapter operation
did not complete'. The clear message (for example apply.yml:152, naming the
object and a remedy) lives only in the root-owned adapter output. The spec
accepts this on purpose (specs/substrates.md:386-389). But the shared protocol
already has a 'refused' phase with a closed reason and detail
(adapter_protocol.py:231-232), used by other roles. This role builds its
capability with no refusals and never emits it. An earlier delivery converted
the tree role's quiet asserts to the refused phase for the same symptom.

**What the operator sees:** Apply failed, [FAIL] substrate-host-\<provider>,
'the adapter operation did not complete', a Logs path, and 'run bootwright
status' as Next. The cause appears only after a privileged bootwright logs.

**Impact:** The most common host-block failures all read the same on stdout.
The operator must open a privileged log to learn which of about 30 causes
fired.

**Recovery today:** Run bootwright logs --context \<c> --operation \<id> with
privilege and read the last fatal line.

**Proposed fix (effort M):** Give the host capability a closed set of refusal
reasons (foreign network, foreign pool, collision, guests running, firewall
not ready, NetworkManager not ready, and so on). Emit the refused phase with
the reason and a bounded detail naming the object before failing. Add the same
reasons to the Go decoder and its message table, so Go reports a named failure
with a remedy.

#### C01-04

**systemctl failures of the routing, VLAN-refusal and firewall-readiness units
drop stderr and name neither the unit nor the step**

Medium · output · both · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/libvirt_routing.py:581-583`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/libvirt_vlan_refusal.py:277-280`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/libvirt_firewall_ready.py:194-197`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/libvirt_nm_connections.py:700-703`

**Scenario:** Apply on a host where the routing unit's start command (nft -f
\<file>) fails, or the readiness unit's 75-second firewall-cmd probe expires
because firewalld is down. require() runs the systemctl step, gets a non-zero
code, throws away stdout and stderr, and raises one fixed text. The same
require() wraps daemon-reload, start, stop, restart and reload in all three
modules, at 16 call sites (routing 6, VLAN refusal 6, readiness 4). All of
them read the same. The readiness variant says 'restore firewalld and repeat'
even when the failing step was daemon-reload. The sibling NetworkManager
module already includes stderr (lines 700-703).

**What the operator sees:** Stdout: 'the adapter operation did not complete'.
Adapter output: 'a routing table operation failed; check systemctl status of
the unit and repeat', with no unit name and no systemd error.

**Impact:** The operator must derive the unit name from the spec's naming rule
and search the host journal by hand. Failures of different steps read the
same.

**Recovery today:** Guess the unit name, run systemctl status and journalctl
-u on the host, fix the cause, repeat apply.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Have require() include the step, the unit name
and a bounded, escaped first line of stderr, as the NetworkManager module does
('nmcli could not %s: %s').

#### C01-05

**Routing-table and VLAN-refusal proofs fold six conditions into one text that
names the table but not which condition failed (rare now).**

Low · output · apply · reported as Medium · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/libvirt_routing.py:617-619`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/libvirt_vlan_refusal.py:322-324`

**What:** After settle() starts the routing unit, the check at
libvirt_routing.py:617-619 joins six conditions (answered, owned, enabled,
active, loaded, forwarding) into one error. The VLAN-refusal settle does the
same for refused routes. In the 2026-11-11 owner run of a network-matrix case,
the table was not loaded and the message did not say so. The cause was found
by hand and fixed under B1335. A failed nft start now fails earlier, inside
require() (C01-04), so only a silent, rare mismatch still reaches this text.
The state is safe: apply fails and a repeat re-settles.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Name the first unmet condition and the unit's
ActiveState in the message, for example 'unit \<name> is \<state>; table inet
\<t> is not loaded'. Do the same for the VLAN-refusal settle (which subnets are
missing or extra). It is the same one change as C01-04, since both sit in the
same helper family.

**Already recorded:** none for the wording; B1335 (delivered) records the
cause found by hand

#### C01-08

**A single unanswered nmcli read after deleting trunks and VLAN legs fails
host removal with a message that reads like a leftover and gives no reason**

Medium · loose end · destroy · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/libvirt_nm_connections.py:827-835`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/libvirt_nm_connections.py:406-416`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/libvirt_nm_connections.py:586-620`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/libvirt_nm_connections.py:487-489`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/libvirt_nm_connections.py:774`

**Scenario:** In one owner destroy run (network-matrix case, 2026-11-12),
remove() deleted the legs and trunks, then re-ran inspect() once at once. The
answer was marked not answered, so line 834 raised. This happens when
profiles() returns None (non-zero exit, or a line without 6 fields, lines
406-416) or when details() fails for a profile still listed (lines 487-489).
The networks, pool and units were not removed. A later destroy finished with
no manual step. links_gone() polls the devices (line 774), but this profile
listing is read once and never retried. Seen once; which branch fired is not
proven.

**What the operator sees:** 'the adapter operation did not complete'. Adapter
output: 'NetworkManager still holds a trunk or VLAN leg after removal: an
nmcli read did not answer'. The same text appears for different causes.

**Impact:** A destroy fails part way and leaves the host safely half-removed
(trunks gone, networks still defined). Repeating completes it, but the message
suggests a real leftover and gives no nmcli exit code or error.

**Recovery today:** Repeat destroy.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Poll the post-removal NetworkManager listing
within a bound, as links_gone does for devices. When it still does not answer,
include nmcli's exit code and a bounded first line of stderr.

#### C01-09

**A hung libvirt daemon makes observe_host fail whole with only a Python class
name, and change modules print a fixed 'could not be changed safely'.**

Low · output · both · reported as Medium · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/bounded_process.py:96-97`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/substrate_libvirt.py:765`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/modules/libvirt_host_inspect.py:57-63`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/modules/libvirt_routing.py:58`

**What:** A libvirt daemon (virtqemud, virtnetworkd or virtstoraged) is
wedged: its socket accepts but it never replies. A virsh call inside
observe_host (substrate_libvirt.py:765-860) runs past COMMAND_SECONDS (300 s),
and bounded_process.py:96-97 raises TimeoutError. observe_host has no try, and
its helpers catch no OSError, so the whole observation fails. The existing
silent-driver design covers non-zero exits, not hangs. The inspect module
reports only type(failure).__name__. The routing, VLAN, readiness and NM
modules print a fixed 'could not be changed safely' for any OSError. The
failure fails closed.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Catch TimeoutError per read in observe_host and
turn it into answered=false for that driver. Report the command's basename and
the bound in module failures, for example 'virsh net-dumpxml did not finish
within 300 s'.

#### C01-10

**policy trade-off: destroy refuses on a silent libvirt driver by design, but
its remedy says 'restore that driver' and names no command.**

Low · output · destroy · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_libvirt_host/tasks/destroy.yml:67`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_libvirt_host/tasks/destroy.yml:83`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_libvirt_host/tasks/apply.yml:114`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_libvirt_host/tasks/apply.yml:130`

**What:** After a host reboot where virtnetworkd was disabled, or after an
operator stopped it, destroy sees the driver silent and refuses
(destroy.yml:60-84). The refusal names virtnetworkd or virstoraged, the
connection, and the network or pool. The spec requires refusing before the
first effect when a driver is silent (specs/substrates.md:465-468), while
apply starts the drivers by design (specs/substrates.md:172-186). So destroy
not starting them is deliberate. What remains is wording: the text says
'restore' and gives no command. The same wording is at apply.yml:114 and :130.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Name 'systemctl start \<daemon>' in the remedy
text, in destroy.yml and in the twin apply.yml refusals. Do not change destroy
to start the drivers, since the spec requires the refusal.

#### C01-11

**Apply stops drifted networks before waiting for the firewall to answer, so a
stopped firewalld leaves them down until a repeat apply.**

Low · loose end · apply · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_libvirt_host/tasks/apply.yml:402-410`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_libvirt_host/tasks/apply.yml:417-427`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_libvirt_host/tasks/apply.yml:429-440`

**What:** An owned network runs a drifted definition and is proved idle.
firewalld was stopped after boot, and the readiness unit stays active
(RemainAfterExit), so libvirt_firewall_ready skips its start. The role runs
net-destroy for the drifted networks (apply.yml:402-410). Only then does it
poll firewall-cmd --state (apply.yml:417-427, 30 retries, 2 s delay) and
refuse at apply.yml:429-440. A stopped firewalld answers 'not running' at
once, so the loop takes about one minute. The 15 s timeout gives about 9
minutes (527 s) only for a hung firewalld.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Move the firewall-answer check before the first
net-destroy, or before any effect, alongside the other refusals.

**Already recorded:** none (B676 does not record it)

### Findings of lane C02

Libvirt machine and emulated BMC (Go capability, role and Python). Lane
summary: [Lane C02](#lane-c02).

#### C02-01

**The libvirt machine role's refusals all reach the operator as 'the adapter
operation did not complete', and the printed remedy points at a root-only
file, not the logs command**

Medium · output · both · reported as High · verified: combined narrowed, reach
narrowed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_libvirt_machine/tasks/apply.yml:39`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_libvirt_machine/tasks/apply.yml:193`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_libvirt_machine/tasks/apply.yml:385`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_libvirt_machine/tasks/destroy.yml:40`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/action/substrate_libvirt_machine_protocol.py:217`,
`internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/process_linux_amd64.go:509`

**Scenario:** An apply reaches block machine-\<m>. A plain assert or fail task
in the role fails. Examples: the pinned image cannot be pulled
(apply.yml:193), the BMC never reports power (apply.yml:385), a same-name
domain is foreign (apply.yml:39), or at destroy the hypervisor is silent
(destroy.yml:40). ansible-playbook exits non-zero, which becomes FailedExit
and then the fixed text 'the adapter operation did not complete'. The
capability is built with the default phases and no named refusals, so the
role's own message reaches only the raw attempt output. The repo already fixed
the same defect for the tree role (specs/milestones/delivered.md:4224-4229).

**What the operator sees:** '! Apply failed', a [FAIL] row naming machine-\<m>,
'lifecycle.state: the adapter operation did not complete', and a remedy shaped
like 'read blocks/\<id>/attempt-N.output in this operation's Logs directory, as
root, for why block \<id> failed'. The same text appears for every cause.

**Impact:** The common causes (image pull through a proxy, silent hypervisor,
BMC without power state) look identical on screen. The role's precise remedies
are discarded. The cause is one documented command away, so the operator is
slowed, not stuck. Medium.

**Recovery today:** Run `bootwright logs --context <c> --block machine-<m>
--raw`. It prints the block's newest retained adapter output, including the
role's own message. Fix the cause and repeat the verb.

**Proposed fix (effort M):** Give the machine capability named refusals
(foreign domain, hypervisor silent, not shut off, image unavailable,
controller silent), as the tree role already has, each naming Machine/\<m>, the
host and the next command. Cheaper partial fix: make the printed remedy name
`bootwright logs --raw --block <id> --attempt <N>`.

**Already recorded:** none (B1079 and Y02-06 are different cases)

#### C02-02

**policy trade-off: a foreign same-name domain blocks apply, and destroy then
fails at the inverse role with the same generic message**

Medium · dead end · both · verified: combined narrowed, arbiter narrowed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_libvirt_machine/tasks/apply.yml:39`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_libvirt_machine/tasks/destroy.yml:50`,
`internal/substrate/libvirt/capability.go:534`,
`specs/state-reconciliation.md:1670`,
`internal/substrate/libvirt/unresolved.go:43`,
`internal/substrate/libvirt/evidence.go:731`

**Scenario:** A provider host holds a domain named bootwright-\<c>-\<m> that is
not this context's (for example from an abandoned same-name context). Apply
asserts at apply.yml:39 before any effect and the attempt is recorded failed,
so the block is failed, not unknown. Destroy does not resolve a failed block.
It registers a removal, because a failed block is still owned. A shut-off
foreign domain passes the quiescence gate (capability.go:534-538). A running
one is refused with a `bootwright machine stop` remedy for a domain this
context does not own. The inverse role then refuses at destroy.yml:50 before
any effect. The unresolved.go:43 and evidence.go:731 path applies only when
the block is unknown, for example after an interrupted apply. The spec
requires both refusals (substrates.md:985-987). The trigger is uncommon.

**What the operator sees:** The generic 'the adapter operation did not
complete' on apply, and again on destroy (see C02-01). The role's own 'remove
or rename' text sits only in the root-owned output. If the foreign domain is
running, destroy shows the machine stop remedy first.

**Impact:** To abandon its own context, the operator must remove or rename
another party's domain, or purge the context, although the apply made no
effect. Medium because the trigger is uncommon.

**Recovery today:** Remove or rename the foreign domain by hand, or `context
delete --purge` (with --allow-orphans). For a running foreign domain the
printed remedy is `bootwright machine stop`.

**Proposed fix (effort M):** Record a positive no-effect attempt when the role
refuses before any effect, or let the removal drop a block whose only finding
is a foreign domain with nothing this context owns present. The change must
reach the removal's inverse and the quiescence gate, not only the resolution.

**Already recorded:** B568 (the same-name identity collision; root cause
only). The generic message on both verbs is C02-01.

#### C02-03

**policy trade-off: a disk attached or detached by hand makes a data-disk
Machine's own domain read foreign, and the destroy remedy tells the operator
to remove or rename it**

Medium · spec gap · both · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/substrate_libvirt.py:539`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/substrate_libvirt.py:595`,
`internal/substrate/libvirt/selection.go:266`,
`internal/substrate/libvirt/projection.go:46`,
`internal/substrate/libvirt/unresolved.go:42`,
`internal/substrate/libvirt/projection_test.go:158`

**Scenario:** A Machine with data disks is realized. Every data disk has a
serial (selection.go:266), so the ownership check compares disk counts
(substrate_libvirt.py:539, 595). The operator attaches an extra disk, or
detaches a declared one, by hand. The count differs, so the domain reads not
owned. Apply and destroy refuse. Destroy resolution says the domain 'does not
carry this context's ownership' and advises 'remove or rename domain'. diff
--observe reads the guest as unknown (projection.go:46). The strict proof for
apply and destroy is deliberate, because removal takes the storage back. The
diff part is parked as B1119. The projection test passes only because its
disks carry no serial.

**What the operator sees:** The generic adapter failure on apply and destroy.
On destroy resolution, 'does not carry this context's ownership' with the
remedy 'remove or rename domain ...'. diff shows the guest as unknown, not the
hand-attached disk.

**Impact:** The remedy tells the operator to remove or rename a domain that is
their own, when the cause is one hand-attached or detached disk. It never
names the disk. That remedy leads to C02-04. Medium.

**Recovery today:** Detach the extra disk by hand (virsh detach-disk --config)
so the disk bindings match again, then repeat. No message says this.

**Proposed fix (effort M):** Give the extra-disk and detached-disk case its
own reason and remedy that names the disk targets. Keep the strict proof for
apply and destroy. Add a Python-to-Go test with serial-bearing data disks plus
an attached one.

**Already recorded:** B1119 (strict proof and the diff read of the guest as
unknown). The misleading remedy text and the detach case are not tracked.

#### C02-04

**Following the 'rename it' remedy on a domain misread as foreign lets destroy
report success while the renamed domain stays defined, and the next apply
likely fails**

Medium · unsafe · destroy · verified: combined narrowed, reach confirmed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/substrate_libvirt.py:528`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_libvirt_machine/tasks/destroy.yml:59`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_libvirt_machine/tasks/destroy.yml:170`,
`internal/substrate/libvirt/capability.go:539`,
`internal/substrate/libvirt/unresolved.go:43`,
`internal/substrate/libvirt/selection.go:221`

**Scenario:** The context's own domain reads foreign after a hand-attached or
detached disk (C02-03). The operator follows the remedy and renames it. The
rename keeps the UUID and the disk sources. Destroy looks the domain up by
name only (substrate_libvirt.py:528), finds nothing, and reads 'not defined'
as quiescent (capability.go:539-540, checked before Power). The role tolerates
'failed to get domain' and deletes the owned disk directory (destroy.yml:170).
Destroy reports done. The renamed domain stays defined, pointing at deleted
images. The UUID is fixed by context and Machine name (selection.go:221), so
the next apply defines the same UUID under the original name. Libvirt is
expected to refuse this, which was not verified in this tree. Renaming a
domain that really is foreign does no harm. Rename needs a shut-off domain, so
the running case needs a deliberate start afterwards.

**What the operator sees:** Destroy succeeds. The later apply fails with the
generic 'the adapter operation did not complete'. Nothing mentions the
leftover renamed domain.

**Impact:** A domain this context created survives a destroy that reported
success, and the next apply is blocked with no cause shown. Disk deletion was
authorized. It needs C02-03 first and the operator following the remedy.
Medium.

**Recovery today:** Run `virsh undefine` on the renamed domain by hand, then
apply.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Make the observation also look up the frozen UUID
(`virsh domname <uuid>`). A domain holding that UUID under another name is
neither absent nor quiescent. Change the remedy wording to 'remove' only,
never 'rename'. Fix together with C02-03.

#### C02-07

**Libvirt apply creates the disk directory and disks before proving the
hypervisor answered, so a silent hypervisor passes the foreign-domain check**

Low · spec gap · apply · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_libvirt_machine/tasks/apply.yml:39-42`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_libvirt_machine/tasks/apply.yml:62`

**What:** The hypervisor does not answer at apply time (libvirtd down, or
virsh fails with something other than 'failed to get domain'). The domain
inspection reports answered=false and an empty domain. The apply check at
apply.yml:39-50 only asserts 'domain is empty or owned', so an empty domain
passes. The role then creates the disk directory (apply.yml:62) and the qcow2
disks, and only then `virsh define` fails. The destroy role
(destroy.yml:37-48) has an explicit 'answered' assert that names this hole.
The apply role has none. The spec (specs/substrates.md:987) says a foreign
domain refuses on apply 'before any effect'.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Add the destroy role's 'Refuse ... a machine its
hypervisor did not answer for' assert, as a named refusal (per C02-01), before
'Create the owned disk directory' in apply.yml.

#### C02-08

**When an owned libvirt domain's state cannot be read, the destroy gate falls
back to the BMC power while the role refuses with a wrong 'stop it' remedy**

Low · output · destroy · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_libvirt_machine/tasks/destroy.yml:67-76`,
`internal/substrate/libvirt/capability.go:541`

**What:** dumpxml answers, but `virsh domstate` fails or prints a word outside
the known states, so the domain state reads as ''. The inspection still
reports answered, present and owned. The Go gate (capability.go:541) skips its
State cases and falls back to the BMC power. If the BMC reports Off, the
machine counts as quiescent and the removal registers. This fallback is
deliberate: capability_test.go:806 pins it. The role (destroy.yml:67-76) does
not see 'shut off' and refuses with 'the machine is not shut off; stop it'.
Trigger: domstate fails while dumpxml and the BMC succeed. This is rare.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Treat an owned, present domain with an unreadable
state as an explicit 'state unreadable' case in the role and say so where the
gate falls back to the BMC. Make the remedy 'check the hypervisor', not 'stop
the machine'.

**Already recorded:** none (delivered.md:453 covers only the down-hypervisor
case)

### Findings of lane C03

Physical machines over Redfish, machine hardware and power. Lane summary:

#### C03-01

**The bare-metal resolution step drops the BMC's error, so a repeat apply with

Medium · output · both · reported as High · verified: combined narrowed, reach

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_baremetal_machine/tasks/observe.yml:35`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/action/substrate_physical_protocol.py:54`,

`internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/process_linux_amd64.go:510`,

**Scenario:** An apply that met an unanswered BMC leaves the claim block

the BMC is still down or refusing, the inspect step (no_log, failed_when
false) gives nothing. observe.yml has no refused phase and no assert on msg,
unlike apply.yml:42-59, and publishes observation | default({}). presence()
reads power None and raises ValueError, so publish returns
capability.unpublished. The runner reports FailedExit: 'the adapter operation
did not complete'. The block stays unknown. capability.go:219 already maps
target-unanswered for every run, but observe.yml never emits it. The same text
appears after an interrupted claim while the BMC is down. Once the BMC
answers, the continuation resolves normally.

**What the operator sees:** The resolution of block machine-\<m> fails with
lifecycle.state 'the adapter operation did not complete'. The remedy points to
a root-owned retained file. That file says only 'the physical machine result
could not be published'. Nothing names the BMC endpoint, the Machine, or that
the BMC did not answer.

**Impact:** Medium. An output defect on the repeat or continuation path only.
The block stays unknown and nothing is unsafe. On that round the operator
cannot tell a dead BMC from a refusing BMC or a Bootwright fault. The first
apply usually already showed the named diagnostic.

**Recovery today:** Restore access to the BMC out of band and repeat apply.
Once the BMC answers, the resolution completes.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Give observe.yml the same refused phase as
apply.yml (reason target-unanswered when the inspect reports unanswered) and
the same msg assert that prints the bounded cause, both before the publish
task. Add a unit test that drives observe.yml with an inspect failure;
test_baremetal_replay.py always supplies an observation.

#### C03-02

**A BMC refusal (401/403/404) or an unloadable trust bundle is reported as
'did not answer' and recorded unknown, and the rebind remedy is never named**

Medium · output · apply · reported as High · verified: combined narrowed,
reach narrowed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/modules/redfish_system_inspect.py:134`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/modules/redfish_system_inspect.py:20`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/redfish_control.py:1167`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_baremetal_machine/tasks/apply.yml:46`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_baremetal_machine/tasks/target_proof.yml:32`,
`internal/substrate/preboot.go:103`

**Scenario:** An operator declares a physical Machine with a wrong or rotated
BMC password, an account without the privilege, a system path that returns
404, or a trust bundle holding a PEM that cannot be loaded. apply reaches
machine-\<m>. The Redfish client raises a ControllerError (a refusal carries
cause=privilege). redfish_system_inspect.py:117-134 wraps the constructor and
the read in one try and sets unanswered=True for every ControllerError except
UnverifiedCertificate. apply.yml and target_proof.yml then name
target-unanswered, Go returns UnansweredTarget (lifecycle.unknown), and the
attempt is recorded unknown. Only status 0 is real silence. The module's own
doc (lines 20-22) says an unloadable bundle fails the module. A refused
certificate is not marked unanswered and fails the apply.yml assert as a plain
task failure. The same mapping covers the pre-boot proof of every bare-metal
installation.

**What the operator sees:** 'lifecycle.unknown: the management controller at
\<endpoint> did not answer the system read for Machine/\<m>', remedy 'read the
controller's cause in the attempt's retained output, restore access and repeat
apply'. The BMC did answer, with 401. The remedy does not name apply
--authorize rebind=\<credentialsRef>.

**Impact:** Medium. The most common onboarding faults on a physical server
read as a network outage. The outcome is unknown, not failed, so the next
apply must resolve first. A repeat apply presents the old bound credential and
stays unknown until the operator finds the rebind option. This also depends on
C03-01. The KubeVirt path names rebind for 401/403.

**Recovery today:** Read the cause with bootwright logs --context \<c> --block
\<machine block> --raw (it shows 'HTTP 401 (\<MessageId>)'). Fix the Secret,
then run apply --authorize rebind=\<secret>. The exit for an unloadable trust
bundle was not verified.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Set unanswered only when nothing answered (status
0). Add a distinct controller-refused refusal for 401/403, as
physical_erase.py already has, that names the Machine, endpoint, HTTP status
and apply --authorize rebind=\<credentialsRef>. Let an unloadable trust bundle
fail the module, as its doc says.

**Also reported as:** X07-02

**Already recorded:** none. Audit 003 finding SBP-11 (an earlier swallowed
read) is a different defect.

#### C03-03

**policy trade-off: a MAC-set mismatch, wrong system or refused certificate in
the claim block shows only 'the adapter operation did not complete'**

Medium · output · apply · reported as High · verified: combined narrowed,
reach narrowed

**Where:** `internal/substrate/baremetal/capability.go:219`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/action/substrate_physical_protocol.py:176`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_baremetal_machine/tasks/apply.yml:51`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_baremetal_machine/tasks/apply.yml:54`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/modules/redfish_system_inspect.py:134`,
`internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/process_linux_amd64.go:510`

**Scenario:** An operator onboards a server and mistypes one NIC's MAC, or
bmc.address points at a neighbouring server. apply runs machine-\<m>. The
inspect succeeds, but completion() returns 'the machine was not proved to be
the one this Machine declares; missing: ...'
(substrate_physical_protocol.py:176). That is a task failure with no refused
phase. For a refused certificate, inspect sets unanswered=False, so the
apply.yml:54 assert fails and its fail_msg carries the cause. Only
target-unanswered is a named refusal (capability.go:219). Both end as
FailedExit with 'the adapter operation did not complete'. The spec
(substrates.md:1365-1368) puts this message in the retained output on purpose.
The claim is not taken.

**What the operator sees:** '! Apply failed', a [FAIL] row for machine-\<m>,
lifecycle.state 'the adapter operation did not complete', and the remedy 'read
\<path> in this operation's Logs directory, as root, for why block machine-\<m>
failed'. The bounded cause is in the retained output, not in the top-level
message.

**Impact:** Medium. Easy to reach on first onboarding and recoverable. The
remedy points at the log holding the exact cause. The machine power path and
the pre-boot proof name the same refusal with an exact remedy, but the claim
block does not, so the product is inconsistent.

**Recovery today:** Run bootwright logs --context \<c> --raw --block
machine-\<m> to print the cause. Then fix the cabling and repeat apply, or
destroy, correct the input, context update and apply.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Emit refused hardware-mismatch and
controller-trust before the publish in apply.yml and register them in
capability.go Refusals, shaped like the pre-boot refusals. Make the remedy
name bootwright logs --raw and the destroy, context update and apply exit.
Note backlog.md:606: an adapter refusal cannot carry names it read, which
limits naming the missing NIC.

**Already recorded:** none. specs/milestones/backlog.md:606 records the
related limit on refusals.

#### C03-04

**A power state that never arrives is reported as the generic 'adapter
operation did not complete', not the lifecycle.unknown with exact commands
that the CLI spec requires**

Medium · spec gap · both · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/action/machine_power_protocol.py:120`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/machine_power/tasks/stop.yml:29`,
`internal/machine/power/evidence.go:47`,
`internal/machine/power/evidence.go:56`,
`internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/process_linux_amd64.go:509`,
`specs/cli.md:1664`

**Scenario:** The operator runs bootwright machine stop --context c --name
ceph-01 --yes on a physical server whose OS ignores the graceful shutdown.
redfish_control.power polls 60 times, then raises 'the system does not report
Off'. The stop.yml assert on msg fails before the publish. Even when
completion() is reached, machine_power_protocol returns (evidence, msg) and
adapter_protocol.handed returns failed without emitting evidence. The runner
ends FailedExit with lifecycle.state 'the adapter operation did not complete'.
The Go branches in evidence.go that return lifecycle.unknown with the --force
remedy run only on published evidence, which the adapter cannot produce for
this case; the test feeds it by hand. The same path covers start and restart,
and every Redfish failure ends in the generic text.

**What the operator sees:** lifecycle.state 'the adapter operation did not
complete' and a pointer to a retained log file. Never the spec's remedy naming
--force or machine list --power-status. The pointer itself is promised by the
spec and is not the defect.

**Impact:** Medium. A graceful stop that the guest ignores is the case the
remedy was written for. The operator is not told about --force, and the
outcome shows as failed although the machine may still be shutting down.

**Recovery today:** Read the run's log file, then repeat with --force.

**Proposed fix (effort M):** Have the power role publish the observed evidence
(postcondition false) when the poll runs out, or name a refused
power-unsettled reason that the runner maps to the existing lifecycle.unknown
diagnostic. Drive one test from the Python poll exhaustion through to the Go
diagnostic.

#### C03-05

**policy trade-off: a failed physical boot leaves inserted media and a
one-time Cd override on the BMC; destroy deliberately touches no BMC and says
nothing about them**

Low · loose end · both · reported as Medium · verified: combined narrowed,
arbiter narrowed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_baremetal_machine/tasks/boot_media.yml:13-24`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_baremetal_machine/tasks/boot_media.yml:57-65`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/managedos_install_anaconda/tasks/apply.yml:414-429`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/managedos_install_anaconda/tasks/apply.yml:500-503`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_baremetal_machine/tasks/destroy.yml:1-39`,
`specs/managed-os.md:649-652`

**What:** A managed-OS install on a bare-metal Machine inserts its image and
sets a one-time Cd boot override (boot_media.yml:13-24). The power-on poll
fails, or the run is canceled (boot_media.yml:57-65). The failure rescue only
reports and fails; it does not eject (apply.yml:414-429). The eject at
apply.yml:500-503 runs only after a successful boot and wait. The operator
then runs destroy. The claim removal makes no BMC call (destroy.yml:1-39).
specs/managed-os.md:649-652 requires that, and says the next apply's eject
settles any leftover. The BMC keeps the image URL and the pending override. A
pending Cd override with the image withdrawn falls through to the disk. A
later insert releases other media itself (redfish_control.py:536-537), and a
later apply sets the override again.

**Proposed fix (effort M):** Optional: add a leftover note to the failed apply
or to the removal result. It names machine eject-media and the pending
one-time override. Do not add a BMC effect to destroy, since the spec forbids
it.

#### C03-06

**policy trade-off: a BMC certificate refused by the bound trust bundle fails
every continuation, as the spec requires, and no message names the exits**

Low · dead end · apply · reported as Medium · verified: combined narrowed,
arbiter narrowed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/redfish_control.py:270-272`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/modules/redfish_system_inspect.py:132-133`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_baremetal_machine/tasks/apply.yml:51-60`,
`specs/secrets.md:405-409`, `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2983-2984`

**What:** An apply registers with a BMC trust bundle bound at one version.
Before the apply finishes, the BMC certificate is re-issued by another CA.
Each attempt raises UnverifiedCertificate (redfish_control.py:270-272). The
inspect does not count it as unanswered (redfish_system_inspect.py:132-133),
so the assert at apply.yml:51-60 stops. The operator updates the Secret and
repeats apply, but the continuation presents the version it bound. The spec
requires this: a trust anchor is never rebound (secrets.md:405-409,
state-reconciliation.md:2983-2984). The only gap is that nothing tells the
operator an updated bundle cannot reach an operation already in flight.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Fold this into the controller-trust refusal that
C03-02 proposes. Its remedy text names restoring the BMC certificate, or
destroy, context update and apply. Allowing a rebind would be a policy change
for the owner.

**Already recorded:** none as an open item; the fix joins the controller-trust
refusal proposed in finding C03-02

#### C03-07

**The root-volume pre-boot refusal is reported as a hardware-address
mismatch**

Low · output · apply · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_baremetal_machine/tasks/target_proof.yml:48`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_baremetal_machine/tasks/target_proof.yml:50-56`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_baremetal_machine/tasks/target_proof.yml:24-27`

**What:** A bare-metal installation declares a logical root volume. Before
media is inserted, the volume read back differs from its durable proof.
target_proof.yml:48 sets the refusal fact to hardware-mismatch
unconditionally, then the root-volume assert at lines 50-56 fails. Nothing
renames the fact in between. The Go side maps hardware-mismatch to the
baremetal diagnostic, which says the machine 'does not report exactly the
hardware addresses ... or its inventory could not be read in full'. The
root-disk refusal at lines 24-27 is mapped to the same label.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Name a 'root-volume-changed' refusal before that
assert, with its own pre-boot refusal entry. The root-disk refusal at lines
24-27 needs the same split. The spec limits hardware-mismatch to MAC and
inventory causes (specs/substrates.md:2288-2320).

#### C03-08

**An SSH-reached server's hardware read failure prints a fixed text and drops
the module's bounded cause, so a failed listing and a failed read look the
same**

Low · output · apply · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/machine_hardware/tasks/apply.yml:29`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/machine_hardware/tasks/observe.yml:29`

**What:** machine-hardware-\<m> runs machine_hardware_read on an OS-ready host.
The read fails, for example on an unreadable sysfs entry. failed_when false at
line 25 hides the module's message. The fail task at line 30 fires when the
addresses are undefined and prints the fixed text at line 29. The runner
returns 'the adapter operation did not complete', which is accurate. The
module's own cause is a fixed, bounded string: 'could not be listed', 'could
not be read in full' or 'a network interface could not be read'. It never
names an interface. specs/substrates.md:1341 requires an unreadable listing to
fail the block.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Surface the module's message
(machine_hardware_read.msg) in the fail message. Optionally add Machine/\<m> to
the diagnostic object. This cannot name the interface, because the module
never does.

#### C03-09

**No test chains a Redfish failure from the power run or the observe entry
point to the Go diagnostic; role-boundary and pre-boot tests cover part of
it**

Low · test gap · both · reported as Medium · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:** `internal/machine/power/evidence_remedy_test.go:50`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/test_baremetal_replay.py:90`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/test_role_boundaries.py:148-166`,

**What:** The power remedy test feeds validate() evidence by hand that the

401-as-unanswered mapping (C03-02) are never run. No golden shows the

test_role_boundaries.py walks observe.yml, apply.yml, stop.yml and power.yml
and simulates a refused controller result at each controller task.
test_pre_boot_refusals.py drives an unanswered inspect to the refusal

### Findings of lane C04

KubeVirt substrate: host, machine and lent access. Lane summary: [Lane
C04](#lane-c04).

#### C04-01

**The KubeVirt arm declares no named refusals, so its lend, machine and host
failures reach the terminal only as 'the adapter operation did not
complete'.**

Medium · output · both · reported as High · verified: combined narrowed, reach
narrowed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_kubevirt_access/tasks/lend.yml:29`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_kubevirt_machine/tasks/apply.yml:42`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_kubevirt_host/tasks/apply.yml:38`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/action/substrate_kubevirt_protocol.py:119`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/action/substrate_kubevirt_protocol.py:120`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/action/substrate_kubevirt_protocol.py:123`

**Scenario:** First apply of a KubeVirt provider whose host has no
ReadWriteMany default class. The lend, machine and host roles use failed_when
false plus an assert whose fail_msg names the object and cause. For an
unproved host the protocol returns a failure message instead of publishing
(substrate_kubevirt_protocol.py:119-120). The KubeVirt Capability declares no
refusals (:123-127), so the task fails and the run exits non-zero. The runner
maps that to 'the adapter operation did not complete'. The Go refusal that
names the failed check and its remedy (evidence.go:95) is reached only from
observation paths. The libvirt roles use the same assert pattern. The tree arm
got the refusal-phase fix (delivered.md:4227).

**What the operator sees:** '! Apply failed', a [FAIL] row naming
substrate-host-\<p> or machine-\<m>, 'the adapter operation did not complete',
and a remedy that names the exact retained output file for that block. The
cause (lend, Machine or provider, and which check) is only in that file.

**Impact:** A wrong storage class, missing namespace or missing RBAC on a
first apply needs an extra step to diagnose. The cause is recoverable, not
hidden. How often this is hit is unmeasured, because the evidence holds no
KubeVirt run.

**Recovery today:** Run bootwright logs --context \<c> --block \<block> --raw
(specs/cli/commands.md:131). It prints the retained output, whose fail_msg
names the host cluster, Machine or provider and the cause. The printed remedy
points at a file path to read as root, not at this command.

**Proposed fix (effort M):** Declare named refusals on the KubeVirt Capability
(for example host-unanswered, foreign-object, frozen-drift, proof-failed,
lend-failed). Have each role emit the refused phase with the reason instead of
an assert. Map each in Go to a diagnostic naming the provider, Machine or host
cluster, with the existing remedies. Point the printed remedy at logs --raw.
Follow the tree-arm fix as precedent.

**Already recorded:** none (the same quiet-assert pattern was fixed for the
tree arm only, delivered.md:4227)

#### C04-02

**When the host cluster is down, a hosted Machine's quiescence probe reports
'could not be read' and names a machine stop that fails the same way, so the
remedy loops.**

Medium · dead end · destroy · verified: combined narrowed, arbiter narrowed

**Where:** `internal/substrate/kubevirt/capability.go:601`,
`internal/substrate/kubevirt/capability.go:606`,
`internal/substrate/kubevirt/capability.go:609`,
`internal/substrate/kubevirt/capability.go:535`,
`internal/substrate/kubevirt/capability.go:541`,
`internal/substrate/kubevirt/capability.go:587`

**Scenario:** A context hosts a KubeVirt provider on a cluster of libvirt
Machines. The host cluster is down, powered off or unreachable. destroy probes
each hosted Machine. The probe's lend cannot reach the host, and any run error
other than cancellation becomes Unproved with the generic reason and Stop set
(capability.go:601-606). The host-aware reason (:609-611) needs a successful
run with no answer, so it is never reached. removal_gates.go builds 'stop it
with bootwright machine stop ..., then repeat'. The hosted stop lends the same
host access (hosted.go:58-66), so with the host down it should fail the same
way. That is inferred from the code and no test pins it. Errors from the
provider proof and the kube-system mismatch are flattened the same way and
lose their own remedies.

**What the operator sees:** Destroy refused: '\<Kind>/\<child> (its
VirtualMachineInstance could not be read)', with the remedy 'stop it with
bootwright machine stop --context \<c> --name \<child>, then repeat ...'. The
stop would then fail reaching the host.

**Impact:** A remedy loop behind an uncommon trigger (a host cluster that is
down). The real exit, starting the host's Machines, is not said. The same
generic reason hides different causes that each need a different exit.

**Recovery today:** Start the host cluster's Machines (bootwright machine
start on the host's libvirt Machines), wait for its API, then repeat destroy.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Classify the run error. Give a lend failure, or
any error on a hosted provider, a Remedy that names starting the host's
Machines (a Remedy suppresses the Stop command). Carry the error's own reason
and remedy for the others. Add a test where the lend fails in the probe.

#### C04-03

**A VirtualMachine edited on the host cannot be destroyed: the observe path
shared by the probe and the removal resolution refuses frozen drift, though
the destroy itself would succeed.**

Medium · dead end · destroy · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/kubevirt_machine.py:635`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/kubevirt_machine.py:619`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/kubevirt_machine.py:685`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/action/substrate_kubevirt_api.py:105`,
`internal/substrate/kubevirt/capability.go:601`,
`internal/substrate/kubevirt/capability.go:603`

**Scenario:** After a completed apply, someone changes the VirtualMachine's
CPU, memory or an interface on the host, and the VM is stopped. destroy runs
the quiescence probe, which plays observe with the shape proof on
(kubevirt_machine.py:635). The proof raises a refusal for the drift (:619).
The probe maps any run error to Unproved 'could not be read'. The stop command
is a no-op on a stopped VM, so destroy refuses again. The removal resolution
(capability.go:482-483) uses the same observe and fails the same way. For a
fresh destroy of an incomplete apply, both observations fail. Yet arm.destroy
reads without the shape proof (:685), and a unit test pins that removal
succeeds. The spec says a removal resolution never refuses on drift
(state-reconciliation.md:706-710).

**What the operator sees:** 'this removal would take back state that is still
in use: Machine/\<name> (its VirtualMachineInstance could not be read)', then
'stop it with machine stop ..., then repeat destroy'. The root-only log says
'destroy and apply again'. After an interrupted removal: 'its observation
returned no evidence'.

**Impact:** No Bootwright exit. The operator must revert the VM spec on the
host by hand, or run context delete --purge --allow-orphans and clean the host
by hand. The trigger is an out-of-band edit, so it is uncommon.

**Recovery today:** Read the root-only log, revert the edited field on the
host, then repeat destroy.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Run the shape proof only for an apply
observation. Either pass the verb into the observe request, or add a
removal-observe mode without the shape proof, matching arm.destroy. Keep the
drift refusal for apply observations.

**Already recorded:** none open. Audit 003 item ADD-15
(audits/003-code/report-final.md) asked that drift never blocks destroy. Its
D233 fix added the observe-time proof without a removal exemption, so this is
a regression from that fix.

#### C04-04

**policy trade-off: a permanently lost host-cluster API blocks deletion of its
own hosted Machines, and the printed remedy loops, leaving only
--allow-orphans over real libvirt objects.**

Medium · dead end · destroy · reported as High · verified: combined narrowed,
reach narrowed

**Where:** `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2426`,
`specs/state-reconciliation.md:2460`,
`internal/substrate/kubevirt/capability.go:631`,
`internal/substrate/kubevirt/capability.go:613`,
`internal/substrate/kubevirt/unresolved.go:69`, `specs/cli/commands.md:138`

**Scenario:** A context builds a host OpenShiftCluster on libvirt Machines and
KubeVirt Machines on it (hostClusterRef). The host's libvirt Machines run, but
its API stays broken for good (lost etcd, or its own disks lost). Hosted
Machines are online removals (capability.go:631-634). The stop proof runs
before registration and returns Unproved when the API does not answer. By the
spec, unknown online cleanup 'cannot admit Machine or substrate deletion'.
destroy takes the whole context and has no waiver. The only waiver,
--unregistered, covers pre-stop guest removal (:2460). The host's libvirt
Machines are never removed.

**What the operator sees:** The quiescence refusal 'its host cluster \<host>
did not answer for its VirtualMachineInstance; start the host's Machines so it
answers, then repeat the destroy'. That remedy loops when the host's Machines
already run. The 'restore the API' remedy (unresolved.go:69) shows only when
destroy follows an incomplete apply.

**Impact:** The only Bootwright exit is context delete --purge
--allow-orphans, which also abandons every libvirt domain, volume and network
of the host. The trigger is narrow: a permanently broken API, which can often
be repaired by hand outside Bootwright.

**Recovery today:** Repair the host cluster by hand, or run context delete
--purge --allow-orphans and remove the libvirt objects by hand.

**Proposed fix (effort M):** Add a recorded waiver to the --authorize model,
like --unregistered. It names the hosted Machines whose online cleanup the
operator abandons because their host cluster is removed in the same destroy.
The engine marks them abandoned with evidence and proceeds. Refuse it when the
host's storage class is external to the host's Machines.

**Already recorded:** related B1181 (two-level nesting only); none for the
single-level broken-host exit

#### C04-05

**A lend that fails while the host is unreachable warns of a leftover Secret
and a minted token, though no token may have been minted**

Low · output · both · reported as Medium · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:** `internal/substrate/kubevirt/lend.go:81`,
`internal/substrate/kubevirt/lend.go:139`

**What:** An apply or destroy attempt on a hosted Machine while the host API
is down. The lend job launched, so the code treats the host as reached
(lend.go:79-83). The lend fails, so the code tries to revoke. The revoke also
cannot reach the host, and it warns on any error (lend.go:138-141). The
warning says the lent token may remain and stays valid until it expires 30
minutes after it was minted. If the token request never ran, that mint cannot
have happened. The code cannot tell a request that was never sent from an
answer that was lost, because the first call is not retried and the failure
kind is not passed to Go. So the Secret may in fact exist. A reachable host
that refuses the request deletes its own Secret, so no warning appears there.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Carry the failure kind (not sent versus answer
lost) from the adapter to Go. Warn only when the Secret may exist. Reword to
'may have been minted' when the outcome is unknown.

**Already recorded:** none (B1230 covers a missing warning for power commands,
a different case)

#### C04-06

**A root DataVolume that does not finish within 300 s fails the apply with no
phase or condition anywhere; this is the apply-time case of the generic
KubeVirt failure message.**

Medium · output · apply · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/kubevirt_machine.py:667`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/kubevirt_machine.py:151`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/kubevirt_machine.py:577`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/kubevirt_machine.py:832`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/action/substrate_kubevirt_protocol.py:87`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/action/substrate_kubevirt_protocol.py:120`

**Scenario:** An apply creates the VirtualMachine. Its root DataVolume stays
Pending or ImportScheduled on a slow or misconfigured class
(WaitForFirstConsumer ignored, a quota, a provisioner down). host.wait returns
the last value after the bound without raising (:151-154). read_machine sets
postcondition false from the DataVolume phase (:577-578) and records only name
and present for volumes, so no phase reaches the evidence. completion()
returns 'the KubeVirt machine did not reach its postcondition', the task
fails, and the runner maps it to the generic message. The block is failed, the
VM exists and no receipts are recorded. diagnosis() exists but is used only
for the power wait (:832).

**What the operator sees:** 'the adapter operation did not complete'. Even the
retained output says only 'the KubeVirt machine did not reach its
postcondition', with no DataVolume name, phase or condition.

**Impact:** The operator cannot tell storage trouble from any other failure
without reading the host directly. Repeating apply waits another 300 s with
the same opaque result.

**Recovery today:** Inspect the DataVolume on the host with oc or kubectl.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** When the wait ends unfinished, raise a refusal
naming DataVolume \<ns>/\<vm>-root, its phase and its first non-True condition
(reuse diagnosis()). It depends on C04-01's named-refusal mechanism. The
evidence shape carries no volume phase, so either raise the refusal in Python
or publish the phase for a Go-side fix.

**Already recorded:** audit 006 finding C04-01 (umbrella for every KubeVirt
arm failure surfacing as the generic message); audit 003 item SBV-15 only
added the gate, not the message

#### C04-07

**The short-token refusal and its remedy are unreachable; a host that caps
token lifetime gets the generic failure**

Low · output · both · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:** `internal/substrate/kubevirt/lend.go:168`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/action/substrate_kubevirt_protocol.py:109`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/kubevirt_access.py:119`,
`internal/substrate/kubevirt/nested_test.go:202`

**What:** A host whose API server caps ServiceAccount token lifetime below the
requested one. bound() returns evidence with the postcondition 'granted >=
seconds', which is false (kubevirt_access.py:119). The publish gate for the
lend (protocol.py:109-111) sends evidence only when the postcondition holds.
Otherwise the task fails with 'the KubeVirt host access was not lent', and no
completed record is emitted. Go sees only a failed exit. So the short-grant
branch (lend.go:167-169), with its remedy 'allow ServiceAccount tokens of at
least \<d> on \<cluster>, or apply again', would need a true postcondition with
a short grant, which is contradictory. The test at nested_test.go:202 builds
that impossible evidence, which is why the branch looks tested. The spec
requires the refusal (substrates.md:1611).

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Let the lend publish its evidence on a short
grant (completion() needs an exemption, since the general publish check is not
used for lend). Or give the failure a named 'token-short' refusal reason that
Go maps to this message.

#### C04-08

**A 401/403 from the KubeVirt host tells every provider to continue with a
rebind of a literal '\<kubeconfig Secret>' placeholder, wrong for hosted and
unhelpful for external**

Low · output · both · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/kubevirt_machine.py:165`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/kubevirt_machine.py:185`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/kubevirt_machine.py:417`,
`substrate_kubevirt_api.py:95`

**What:** On a hosted provider, a machine apply or destroy gets 403 because
the kubevirt add-on's Role lacks a verb, or 401 because the lent token was
revoked early. answered_reason (kubevirt_machine.py:163-167) returns the
rebind text for every 401/403, with no hosted branch. Hosted providers get
access from a lend, so there is no bound kubeconfig Secret to rebind, and the
rebind would be refused. The right remedy is the host's kubevirt add-on roles,
or repeating, since each run mints a new token. The external case also shows
the literal '\<kubeconfig Secret>' instead of the real name, which Go knows.
The proof path shows the text in the provider-proof diagnostic
(evidence.go:94-95). The apply and destroy path puts it only in the retained
log. The Go side already splits the hosted case (unresolved.go:67-71). The
only test pins the rebind wording.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Pass whether the access is lent into the host or
client, and word the hosted case: 'the token lent from OpenShiftCluster/\<h>
was refused; check the kubevirt add-on's roles in namespace \<ns> and repeat'.
Name the real Secret in the external case.

Managed OS installation (Anaconda): apply, completion proof, observe and
