**What:** RegistryAuth returns three different errors: the pull secret is not
JSON (:19), it holds no quay.io token (:28), and the mirror credential is
empty or equals the origin (:31). lendReleaseAuth discards the error
(releases_custody.go:37-40) and always reports that the pull secret holds no
quay.io entry. A pull secret that is not valid JSON, for example a pasted file
with a BOM or trailing garbage, gets a message saying the quay.io entry is
missing. ProveCredential at line 22 runs first and pre-empts the
empty-credential case. Nothing checks the pull secret is JSON when it is
stored (secrets/values.go:135 only lists the parts).

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Return a typed error from RegistryAuth for each
case and map each to its own message, such as "is not a registry auth
document" and "names no quay.io auth token".

#### C14-07

**The plan-time request check reuses "frozen request ... destroy it with the
build that applied it" for a request that was never frozen, in all three
fills**

Low · output · apply · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:** `internal/infrastructureservices/mirrorfill/requests.go:74`,
`internal/infrastructureservices/mirrorfill/releases_requests.go:105`,
`internal/infrastructureservices/mirrorfill/images_requests.go:63`,
`internal/infrastructureservices/mirrorfill/capability.go:136`,
`internal/infrastructureservices/mirrorfill/releases.go:110`

**What:** On a fresh context, the build's acquisition list yields a mirror
file with a non-https source, more than 128 files, or a release whose client
URL contains '?'. Files.Request (capability.go:136) and ReleaseFill.Requests
(releases.go:110) build the request at plan time and call validate().
validate() returns the refusal about a "frozen" request. Nothing was applied,
so "destroy it with the build that applied it" has no meaning. The decode path
(requests.go:67, releases_requests.go:91) calls the same validate(). The same
text is in images_requests.go:63.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** At plan time use an internal-error message, or
one naming the offending artifact, for all three request kinds. Keep the
"frozen" text only for the decode path. The golden file for the files fill
pins a different "malformed" text for the decode path only, so nothing pins
the plan-time message.

#### C14-08

**The generic postcondition refusal names no object, carries no remedy, and
pairs code lifecycle.state with an unknown outcome**

Low · output · both · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:** `internal/infrastructureservices/mirrorfill/fill.go:166`,
`internal/diagnostics/remediation.go:74`

**What:** fill.go:166-168 returns an unknown outcome with a lifecycle.state
refusal, an empty remedy and no object. The condition also covers a run
outcome that is not settled with no error. So a plain failed run can be
labelled "did not prove its postcondition". Other triggers are an evidence
digest or version mismatch, or a decoded effect that is not completed.
diagnostics/remediation.go:74 then supplies the default remedy.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Attach the block's object identity and say which
proof failed: unsettled outcome, evidence decode error, or effect. Use
lifecycle.unknown to match the recorded outcome. The golden
fill-behaviour-files.golden:145-149 pins the current text, so update it with
the fix.

### Findings of lane C15

Add-ons: instances, cluster objects and packages. Lane summary: [Lane
C15](#lane-c15).

#### C15-01

**policy trade-off: an add-on refusal that names the object reaches the
operator only as 'the adapter operation did not complete'; the cause sits in
retained output**

Medium · output · apply · reported as High · verified: combined narrowed,
reach narrowed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/action/cluster_objects_protocol.py:19`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/action/cluster_objects_write.py:41`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/cluster_objects/tasks/apply.yml:47`,
`adapterprotocol/process_linux_amd64.go:307`,
`internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/process_linux_amd64.go:509`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/invocation.go:272`

**Scenario:** Apply, add-ons stage. The cluster object engine raises its
Refused exception, for example a Namespace that exists without the owner mark,
a deadline reached, a field that differs, or a CSV pin missing from the
catalog. The write plugin turns it into a failed result and the play's rescue
prints the message, then ansible-playbook exits non-zero. The adapter session
ends as FailedExit, which the lifecycle judge maps to the generic text. Only a
named Refusals entry replaces it (process_linux_amd64.go:421-427). The add-on
capability and driver.Run set none, so the object and field never reach
stdout, stderr or status. The cluster network block shares this adapter.

**What the operator sees:** [FAIL] install add-on \<name> on \<cluster>;
'lifecycle.state: the adapter operation did not complete'; remedy 'read
\<relative path> in this operation's Logs directory, as root, for why block
\<id> failed'. The object and field appear only in the retained output.

**Impact:** Medium. The operator learns the cause only after one extra step. A
transient wait and a deterministic refusal look the same, so the operator
cannot tell whether a retry will fail again. The spec deliberately limits the
cause to retained output.

**Recovery today:** Run `bootwright logs --raw --block <id>` for the failed
block, read the ansible fail message, then correct the cluster or destroy. No
direct read of root-owned files is needed.

**Proposed fix (effort M):** Extend the existing rule that every lifecycle
refusal reaches the operator as its own diagnostic to the cluster object
capability. Give it a closed set of refused reasons and emit a refused record
with a bounded kind, namespace, name and field detail. Cheaper partial fix:
point the FailedExit remedy at `bootwright logs --raw --block <id>`.

**Already recorded:** B251 (every lifecycle refusal reaches the operator as
its own diagnostic; delivered in tree, awaiting acceptance, not applied to
cluster objects). Related: B1415 (specified the refusal in retained output
only), B1233 (log records why).

#### C15-02

**policy trade-off: an add-on object that could not be read shares the
foreign-object reason, and its remedy tells the operator to destroy and apply
again**

Medium · output · apply · reported as High · verified: combined narrowed,
reach narrowed

**Where:** `internal/addons/instance/unresolved.go:14`,
`internal/addons/instance/unresolved.go:19`,
`internal/addons/instance/unresolved.go:30`,
`internal/addons/instance/unresolved.go:32`,
`internal/addons/instance/unresolved.go:83`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/unresolved.go:116`

**Scenario:** An add-on block is unknown or running after an interrupt. The
operator repeats apply while the cluster API does not answer. Every oc read
fails and returns 'not answered'. In observe mode the engine records ownership
'unknown', and the observation completes. The resolution then returns the
shared reason 'is foreign or could not be read' with the destroy-and-apply
remedy. An instance added by an additive apply gets 'remove or correct the
object on the cluster...' or 'leave the object: ... correct the input of that
add-on'. All three are wrong for an unreadable object. This is uncommon and
needs an API outage at observation time.

**What the operator sees:** lifecycle.unknown: the outcome of
addon-gitops-\<cluster> is still unknown: Namespace//\<name> is foreign or could
not be read; destroy and apply again, then repeat bootwright apply --context
\<ctx> to observe it again. A cluster-scoped kind shows an empty namespace
segment (a separate cosmetic defect).

**Impact:** Medium. The remedy is wrong for an unreadable object, but the text
says 'could not be read' and ends with 'then repeat apply'. The operator is
not forced to tear down.

**Recovery today:** Wait until the cluster API answers and repeat apply. The
next resolution observes the block again.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Split the reason by the evidence's Ownership.
Unknown: 'could not be read from cluster \<cluster>', remedy 'make the cluster
API reachable with its kubeconfig and repeat apply'. Foreign: keep the current
text. The spec requires today's text, so change specs/add-ons.md:463-470, the
delivered record B750 and docs/operator-guide.md:828-830 together, and the
networking reason.

#### C15-03

**Every oc failure becomes 'not answered', so an apply waits the whole
readiness budget on a permanent error such as 401, 403 or x509 and reports
only 'read unknown'**

Medium · output · apply · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_native.py:101`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_native.py:151`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py:89`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py:69`

**Scenario:** The kubeconfig in custody stops working, for example the client
certificate is rejected after a CA change, or RBAC forbids reads. get() runs
oc, which exits non-zero with Unauthorized, Forbidden or an x509 error. Any
non-zero exit except the unserved-type text returns answered:false, and run()
drops stderr, so the cause is lost. probe(wait=True) then pauses '\<object>
read unknown' every 10 s until the add-on budget ends and raises 'deadline
reached: ... read unknown'. No classifier exists. Waiting on an unreadable API
is required by the spec (add-ons.md:286-288).

**What the operator sees:** After the full budget (30 minutes or more):
'lifecycle.state: the adapter operation did not complete'. The raw output says
'deadline reached: \<Kind>/\<ns>/\<name> read unknown' with no cause.

**Impact:** Medium. A permanent credential or permission error costs as long
as a flapping API, on every retry. The cause class (credential, reachability,
TLS, RBAC) is visible nowhere.

**Recovery today:** Guess the cause, test oc by hand with the root-owned
kubeconfig, then repeat apply.

**Proposed fix (effort M):** Classify oc's stderr into a closed cause set
(unreachable, timeout, unauthorized, forbidden, tls, unserved type, other).
Keep retrying the transient ones, fail fast on unauthorized, forbidden and
tls, and report the class, never the text, in the refusal detail and the
observation evidence.

#### C15-04

**A readable CSV in any phase that is not Succeeded is reported with the last
observation 'Succeeded', so the deadline message claims success**

Medium · output · apply · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py:231`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py:343`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py:69`

**Scenario:** The pinned CSV metallb-operator.vX is installed but stays in any
other phase (Failed, Installing, Pending), for example because an operator
deployment cannot pull its image in a disconnected lab. csv() returns (False,
'Succeeded') because the CSV object is readable. subscription() pauses with
'Subscription/\<ns>/\<name> Succeeded' and at the deadline raises 'deadline
reached: Subscription/\<ns>/\<name> Succeeded'. A csvSucceeded check records
satisfied:false with lastObservation 'Succeeded'. Nothing else reads the phase
on this path.

**What the operator sees:** In bootwright logs --raw: 'deadline reached:
Subscription/metallb-system/metallb-operator-sub Succeeded', a failure message
that claims success.

**Impact:** Medium. It misleads on a common add-on failure, an operator that
never becomes ready, and points away from the CSV phase that is the real
cause.

**Recovery today:** Read the CSV phase on the cluster by hand.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Return the bounded CSV phase
(model.native(phase)) as the last observation, and 'pending' only when the
phase is empty. Add a unit test that drives Installing and Failed phases to
the deadline and asserts the text.

#### C15-05

**A plain readiness or catalog-gate deadline names the unmet checks by
position ('check 3: False'), not by object or condition**

Medium · output · apply · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py:238`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py:242`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py:247`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py:579`,
`test_cluster_objects.py:480`, `test_cluster_objects_scope_gate.py:48`

**Scenario:** An fdf instance waits for StorageCluster Available, or a
mirrored CatalogSource never reaches READY. Engine.checks builds 'check %d:
%s' from the check index and the last observation and passes it to pause, so
the deadline reads 'deadline reached: check 3: False'. For a gate the checks
are not stored, so the index is only the offset plus the position. A failure
condition already raises with the object label (line 213), so only the plain
deadline is anonymous.

**What the operator sees:** In the raw output only: 'deadline reached: check
3: unknown; check 4: absent'. No object kind, name, condition type or status
path.

**Impact:** Medium. The operator cannot map 'check 3' to anything they
declared or can inspect. The spec says the attempt fails 'naming each unmet
check and its last observation' (add-ons.md:413), so index-only text is a
partial miss.

**Recovery today:** Read the frozen request in plan.json and count the checks
by hand.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Render each unmet check as '\<Kind>/\<ns>/\<name>
\<checkKind> \<type or path>: \<last>' from the check value already in hand,
bounded like other refusals. Update the two tests that pin the 'check N:'
format.

#### C15-06

**Receipts published before a failed add-on apply attempt are dropped, so a
retry cannot use them, contrary to the spec's receipt-continuity sentence**

Low · spec gap · apply · reported as Medium · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:** `internal/addons/instance/capability.go:132`,
`internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/process_linux_amd64.go:509`,
`internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/process_linux_amd64.go:510`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/action/cluster_objects_write.py:47`

**What:** An apply attempt creates the Namespace, OperatorGroup and
Subscription, and each gets a uid receipt. The action publishes the receipts
before it fails (cluster_objects_write.py:47). The attempt then refuses, for
example on a deadline or a plan proof mismatch, and the task fails.
ansible-playbook exits nonzero, so the session ends with a failed exit that
carries no evidence. The judge returns an empty result
(process_linux_amd64.go:509-510). Capability.Apply then records nil evidence
(capability.go:132). On retry there are no receipts, so ownership falls back
to the owner mark plus creation time.

**Proposed fix (effort M):** Let a failed exit that follows a valid completed
record carry that record's evidence to the capability. Alternatively emit a
refused record with evidence, and have Capability.Apply keep it as the
attempt's evidence with outcome failed.

**Already recorded:** none (audit 001 finding F10-08 is related context: it
accepted recording the mark basis)

#### C15-08

**A refused operand create loses the API's reason: stderr is dropped and the
engine reports only "create unproved: absent" for denials, invalid objects and
conflicts.**

Medium · output · apply · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_native.py:177-178`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py:131-150`

**Scenario:** A program creates an operand custom resource with oc create and
the API refuses it. Causes include an admission webhook denial (Forbidden or
Invalid), an invalid object, or a conflict. A client-side mapping miss from a
lagging API server is a possible cause, but it was not shown to occur: the
gate that checks the CRD is being served narrows that window. The create
returns retryable only when the status reason is InternalError or
ServiceUnavailable (transient_status), so the refusal is final. The re-probe
finds the object absent, and the engine raises '\<Kind>/\<ns>/\<name> create
unproved: absent'. The oc stderr holding the reason is discarded.

**What the operator sees:** 'the adapter operation did not complete'. The raw
output says '\<Kind>/\<ns>/\<name> create unproved: absent' with no reason. The
message is the same for a webhook denial, an invalid object, a mapping miss
and a conflict.

**Impact:** A deterministic refusal, such as a webhook policy denial, cannot
be told apart from any other refused create, and the operator cannot see why
it failed. The lost reason is the verified defect.

**Recovery today:** No command shows the reason, because the discarded stderr
is the only source. Repeat apply if a transient cause is suspected. For a
denial, the operator has to reproduce the create by hand with oc.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Return a closed reason class (Forbidden, Invalid,
AlreadyExists, Conflict, mapping) in the refusal detail instead of discarding
stderr. Retrying the mapping miss is a separate choice: the spec at
specs/add-ons.md:289-295 limits retries to InternalError and
ServiceUnavailable, so amend the spec first if that retry is wanted.

#### C15-09

**Run-time refusals of a frozen add-on request name remedies that do not
apply, although the current build can retire the instance**

Low · output · apply · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:** `internal/addons/instance/placements.go:16`,
`internal/addons/instance/placements.go:21`,
`internal/addons/instance/placements.go:24`,
`internal/addons/instance/placements.go:98`

**What:** An operation frozen by an earlier build is continued or observed
(diff --observe) by a build whose registry dropped or changed the package.
validateNamespaces runs only from run(), reached by Apply and Observe
(capability.go:189). It refuses with 'select a built-in package', or with
'destroy the operation with the build that froze it, or plan again with this
build'. Selection is frozen in the plan. An incomplete apply continues its
frozen plan, so 'plan again' is no exit. Destroy, ObserveRemoval and Quiescent
only decode the request (capability.go:158-183), so the current build can
retire the instance. The refusal is right. The remedy is wrong.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Change the remedy to name destroy with the
current build, for example 'destroy the operation (this build retires it),
then apply again'. Tests only assert that a remedy exists
(placement_namespaces_test.go:138-142), so none blocks the change.

#### C15-10

**An add-on observation whose evidence fails Go validation swallows the error
and shows the generic 'restore the target' remedy**

Low · output · apply · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:** `internal/addons/instance/capability.go:154`,
`internal/addons/instance/capability.go:146`,
`internal/addons/instance/unresolved.go:67`,
`evidence.go:57`

**What:** The observe adapter completes, but its evidence fails DecodeEvidence
(another version or digest, or a native value ValidateEvidence refuses).
SafeEvidence returns nil (driver/evidence.go:57-62) and effectOf errors on
empty evidence. Observe returns EffectUnknown with a nil error
(capability.go:154), so the engine sees no observation failure. Unresolved
decodes the nil evidence, fails, and returns false (unresolved.go:67-69). The
engine then uses the generic 'unexplained' text. capability_test.go:175 pins
this nil error, so the swallow is deliberate.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Return the decode error as an observation failure
(resolution observation-failed) so the cause text is recorded. This changes
behavior pinned by capability_test.go:175, so that test must change too.
Alternatively let Unresolved report a reason for empty evidence.

### Findings of lane C16

Custom playbooks, network, machine access, SSH identity and host-key trust
inside a run. Lane summary: [Lane C16](#lane-c16).

#### C16-01

**The Machine identity read drops the SSH cause (host key, refused key,
timeout) and fails with one generic message after an hour, naming neither
Machine nor address**

Medium · output · apply · reported as High · verified: combined narrowed,
reach narrowed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/machine_ssh_identity/tasks/main.yml:36-45`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/machine_ssh_identity/tasks/main.yml:47-58`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/managedos_install_anaconda/tasks/identity_until_answered.yml:16-28`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/modules/managedos_guest_command.py:154`,
`internal/managedos/installation/catalog.go:35`,
`internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/process_linux_amd64.go:510`

**Scenario:** Applies to arms that deliver a host key: bare metal, and libvirt
with hostKeyRef. The libvirt agent channel is separate. The wait starts only
after the installer powered the machine off and the installed disk was booted.
The address then answers with another host key (an address collision, or
firmware booting another disk), or refuses the fleet key (a missing delivered
key, which needs a Bootwright kickstart defect). The guest command returns rc
255 with ssh's stderr. The read runs under no_log with failed_when false and
retries on any non-zero rc for 120 attempts of 30 s, one hour. The role
publishes only answered, marker and host_key, so rc and stderr are dropped.
The assert then fails with one text for every cause.

**What the operator sees:** After about an hour: '! Apply failed', a [FAIL]
row for the os-install block, 'lifecycle.state: the adapter operation did not
complete', and the log text 'the machine never answered with an install marker
... within 120 attempts over 3600 seconds'. The same text appears for a
machine that never booted. The apply output was not reconstructed beyond the
runner mapping. The text names neither the Machine, the address nor the cause.

**Impact:** The operator cannot tell a different host at the address, or a
refused key, from a machine that is still installing or powered off. They wait
an hour for a failure ssh reported at once. Uncommon, so Medium. The common
never-answers cases are correctly retried and correctly worded.

**Recovery today:** Inspect the host by hand, on the console or with a manual
ssh using the fleet key. Repeating apply does not help: the install was never
proved, so the pre-boot identity read fails the same way, the machine counts
as not installed, and apply reinstalls it and waits another hour.

**Proposed fix (effort M):** Publish the last cause class of an unanswered
read (host key, auth, refused, no route, timeout). Reuse the existing
classifiers in managedos_guest_ssh.py:52-56 and
physical_erase_controller.py:63. Name Machine, address and class in the
assert. Stop early only on auth, or on a host-key mismatch that persists for a
few attempts, not the first, since a collision can clear.

#### C16-03

**Policy trade-off: a placement host whose key changed after binding strands
its operation, because a knownHostsRef trust anchor is never rebound**

Medium · dead end · both · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:** `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2982-2983`,
`specs/secrets.md:405-410`,
`internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/runner.go:155`,
`internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/runner.go:164`,
`specs/state-reconciliation.md:1878-1884`

**Scenario:** Apply completes a managed service on a provided SSH host whose
knownHostsRef version V1 is bound with the plan. The host is later re-imaged
or its host keys are regenerated. The operator runs destroy. By the spec, a
removal presents the version its operation bound (secrets.md:405-410), so the
runner reads V1 from request.Material (runner.go:155) and pins it
(runner.go:164). That the removal presents the apply's bound version rests on
the spec sentence, not on code read. ssh refuses the new key. The operator
authors V2 and runs `context update`, but the removal still presents V1.
`--authorize rebind=<ref>` refuses trust anchors, and the lost-binding exits
do not apply because V1 is still readable. The spec names this exclusion on
purpose.

**What the operator sees:** 'lifecycle.state: the adapter operation did not
complete' on every destroy and apply repeat. That generic text appears only
when ssh refuses the key (see the sibling finding C16-02). Nothing says the
changed key is the cause, that the pinned key is the bound version, or that it
cannot be changed.

**Impact:** The removal has no Bootwright exit. Uncommon trigger (a provided
host re-imaged or re-keyed after apply), so Medium.

**Recovery today:** Restore the old sshd host key on the host and repeat,
possible only if the old private key survives. Or run `context delete --purge
--allow-orphans` and clean the service's units, containers and firewall rules
from the host by hand.

**Proposed fix (effort M):** A new capability: the rebind spec
(state-reconciliation.md:2947-2995) would need an exception for trust anchors.
Allow `--authorize rebind=<knownHostsRef>` only with `--expect
\<machine>=SHA256:\<fingerprint>`, proven out of band as `machine trust
--replace` already does. Record old and new pins in the operation log.

#### C16-04

**The SSH placement arm does not admit the pinned key type against the
controller's crypto policy, unlike sessions, installations and Ceph**

Medium · spec gap · both · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:** `internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/process_linux_amd64.go:272`,
`internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/runner.go:145-176`,
`specs/cli.md:1380-1384`

**Scenario:** The controller runs a crypto policy that excludes the pinned key
type, for example FIPS with an ssh-ed25519 key. A provided placement host's
knownHostsRef pins such a key. Plan and registration succeed: checkHostKey
(runner.go:145-176) checks only the Secret's form and that the entry parses,
and no step checks the key type against policy. The runner only writes an
Include of the crypto-policy file (process_linux_amd64.go:272) and passes no
HostKeyAlgorithms. At run time ssh is inferred, from OpenSSH behaviour and not
proved in code, to exit 255. Any non-zero ansible-playbook exit maps to the
generic failure.

**What the operator sees:** 'lifecycle.state: the adapter operation did not
complete' after registration, for every block on that host. A `machine exec`
to the same Machine instead refuses before connecting with access.unavailable
naming the Machine, the key type and the remedy (cli.md:1380-1384).

**Impact:** A predictable configuration conflict shows up only after
registration and only as a generic failure. The same build classifies it
precisely for sessions, for installations (key_policy.go) and for Ceph
(sshPolicyRefusals). It needs a policy that excludes the key type.

**Recovery today:** Read the raw log, recognize the algorithm negotiation
failure, and re-author knownHostsRef with a key type the policy admits. The
Secret is re-authored and bound again.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Reuse sshlocal's HostKeyAlgorithms admission (the
`ssh -G` intersection) in the runner's checkHostKey. Refuse with
access.unavailable naming Machine/\<m>, the key type and the remedy before the
job is written, and pass -o HostKeyAlgorithms=\<intersection> as sessions do.
Better, run the same check at plan time.

#### C16-05

**No test drives an SSH host-key refusal or an unreachable host through the
machine SSH identity role or the runner, so the operator-facing result is
unpinned.**

Low · test gap · both · reported as Medium · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/machine_ssh_identity/tasks/main.yml:23`,
`internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/runner.go:79`

**What:** No role-level or runner-level test makes ssh reject a live host key,
refuse a key, or report the host unreachable inside an apply or destroy block.
The role unit tests check boundaries and argument specs. The runner tests
check the Secret form
(TestAnSSHPlacementRefusesKnownHostsNotOneEntryForItsHostBeforeItConnects) but
not what the operator sees when ssh rejects a key. Two things are already
pinned and are not part of the gap. A failed exit reports 'the adapter
operation did not complete' (process_linux_amd64_test.go:230-233 and :886). An
unanswered machine is never read as released
(test_managedos_install_observation.py:205-228). A nonzero return code gives
answered=false at tasks/main.yml:49-51.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Add a role-level test with a fake ssh that
returns 255 with 'Host key verification failed' (and one with 'Permission
denied'). Assert that the role gives answered=false with an empty marker and
host key. Add a runner test whose fake ansible reports UNREACHABLE and assert
the classified diagnostic. Do not assert that the loop stops at once: the role
retries until attempts pass the retry count (main.yml:40-42).

### Findings of lane C17

Shared adapter plumbing: playbook structure, protocol emitter, censoring and
bounded processes. Lane summary: [Lane C17](#lane-c17).

#### C17-01

**policy trade-off: a role's own failure message reaches only root-only raw
output; the CLI prints one fixed line and a Next that can contradict the
role's remedy**

High · output · both · verified: combined confirmed, reach confirmed

**Where:** `internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/process_linux_amd64.go:510`,
`internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/process_linux_amd64.go:422-429`,
`internal/adapterprotocol/process_linux_amd64.go:308`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/invocation.go:272`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/attempts.go:743`,
`internal/reconciliation/operationstore/records.go:208-209`

**Scenario:** No operator mistake is needed. Any role fail or assert, or any
module error, makes ansible-playbook exit non-zero. The runner then sets a
failed-exit ending and returns the fixed text "the adapter operation did not
complete". Only a `refused` record carries a role-named cause, and most role
stops do not publish one. The anaconda rescue publishes it only when a refusal
is set; otherwise it fails with "the failed step above names what refused".
Adapter output goes only to the retained output file, which only `bootwright
logs` shows. The failed attempt stores no cause, and `status` shows none for a
[FAIL] block. The architecture spec makes the failed exit generic on purpose
(architecture.md:974, 1079-1081).

**What the operator sees:** `! Apply failed`, a [FAIL] row per block,
`lifecycle.state: the adapter operation did not complete`, then `read
operations/.../attempt-000001.output in this operation's Logs directory, as
root, for why block \<id> failed`, and `Next bootwright apply --context \<c>`.
Status later shows [FAIL] with no reason. The golden shows no cause.

**Impact:** The most common failure class needs a root read of raw Ansible
output to diagnose. Role authors already wrote exact causes and remedies, and
the operator never sees them. The generic Next says repeat apply even where
the role says destroy first, so an attempt can repeat the same failure.

**Recovery today:** Run `bootwright logs --context <c> --operation <op>` as
root (or `--raw --block <id>`) and find the first `fatal:` or `[ERROR]` line.
Follow the role's remedy, not the printed Next.

**Proposed fix (effort M):** Add a bounded `failed` record from the censored
callback for the first failing task that is not no_log, carrying task name and
message. Go appends it to the failed-exit diagnostic as the cause. Or convert
role stops that name a remedy into named `refused` reasons. Keep the generic
text as a fallback.

**Also reported as:** E10-01, O09-01, O10-01, X16-01, O04-03, X08-03

**Already recorded:** Partly B1233 (the attempt-log reason only). Its proposed
first diagnostic line would be the same generic text, so the fix must carry
the role's own message.

#### C17-02

**A failed completion's message naming the unproved fields is censored by its
task's no_log, so no output says what was not proved, against the spec's
promise**

High · output · both · verified: combined narrowed, reach narrowed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/adapter_protocol.py:72`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/adapter_protocol.py:69`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/adapter_protocol.py:247-249`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/adapter_protocol.py`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/callback/censored.py:53-57`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_libvirt_host/tasks/apply.yml:561`

**Scenario:** A role runs all its effects, but the final check does not prove
a postcondition. The completion task (for example the libvirt host publish
task at apply.yml:561) runs with no_log. The protocol plugin builds a message
naming the unproved fields (adapter_protocol.py:72) and returns {failed, msg}
without emitting a record (:249). ansible-core drops msg from a no_log result,
and the censored callback strips the raised keys. The runner sees a non-zero
exit and prints the generic text. Only 5 completions are allowed to print
(test_role_boundaries.py:57-63, :358). A repeated apply is a working exit, so
this is not a dead end.

**What the operator sees:** `the adapter operation did not complete`. Even the
root-only output shows only the task name (for example `Publish bounded
installation observation evidence`) FAILED with the censored placeholder. For
an observation, `observation-failed` and then an unknown result.

**Impact:** After the effects ran, nothing anywhere, not even root-only logs,
says which postcondition field was unproved. The operator cannot tell whether
repeating will help. The evidence holds 4 such censored failures. The
architecture spec promises the field names stay visible where evidence is
censored (architecture.md:1097-1099), and that promise is unmet.

**Recovery today:** Repeat `bootwright apply`, which re-runs the effects and
may converge. Otherwise check the host or cluster by hand. No Bootwright
output names the fields.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** On a completion failure, emit a closed `refused`
record with a protocol reason (for example postcondition-unproved) and the
unproved field names as detail. Or print the message outside the result, as
controller_refusal does for its warnings. Add a test that the field names
reach the Go diagnostic.

**Also reported as:** X10-01, C01-02, C08-03, O07-03

**Already recorded:** B245 (specs/milestones/backlog.md:586, parked since X32:
"completion refusals that name only fields ... now print nowhere"). Its exit
evidence, a decision per refusal, owns the fix. B1089 (no_log masking of
non-secret values) is a separate cause of some cited runs.

#### C17-03

**Plain refusals in controller tool preparation (bundle entry ownership,
acquisition process, early request checks) reach the operator only as the
generic controller.install failure.**

Low · output · apply · reported as Medium · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/action/controller_tool.py:60`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/action/controller_tool.py:80`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/controller_refusal.py:35`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/controller_batch.py:126`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/controller_batch.py:160`,
`internal/controller/ansiblelocal/runner_linux_amd64.go:333`

**What:** The controller stage runs controller_prerequisites, and
controller_tool calls prepare_tools. A plain Refused is raised for 'bundle
entry ownership' (controller_files.py:941), for 'acquisition process' (a
worker exits non-zero; controller_batch.py:126 and :160-162), or for a request
refused before acquisition. record() returns None for a plain Refused, and
name() warns only for an AcquisitionRefused (controller_refusal.py:35). The
action returns failed under no_log. The run ends FailedExit, and Go reports
the generic controller.install text. A system TLS trust refusal inside the
worker is already recorded as class 'trust'. A 'proxy bypass' refusal is a
malformed-rule check, not a fixable host condition. The triggers need a
hand-edited bundle or a worker crash. The spec says an internal refusal keeps
the generic failure (architecture.md:1002).

**Proposed fix (effort S):** For every plain Refused, emit a controller
refused record with reason `internal` and a closed detail naming the class
(the strings are fixed and value-free). The controller runner then appends the
detail to its generic diagnostic. This is the correction audit 003 finding
CTS-08 already gives.

**Already recorded:** B1092 (backlog.md:2959, parked; it names this gap:
refusals outside acquisition reach the operator only as the generic
controller.install remedy) and audit 003 finding CTS-08.

#### C17-04

**A request refused before the adapter's `loaded` record (argument spec or
frozen-request assert) reads as the generic failed operation, with no hint
that no effect ran.**

Low · output · both · reported as Medium · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:** `internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/process_linux_amd64.go:385`,
`internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/process_linux_amd64.go:509`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_libvirt_host/tasks/apply.yml:13`

**What:** The Go request encoding and a role's argument spec or version assert
disagree, which is a shipped build defect that tests are meant to catch
(architecture.md:889-893). The argument-spec validation or the no_log
'Validate the frozen ... request' assert fails before the loaded record, so
j.loaded stays false (process_linux_amd64.go:383-386). result() maps
FailedExit to the fixed text 'the adapter operation did not complete' without
checking j.loaded (:509). The attempt is recorded as failed
(invocation.go:299-308). A repeat apply fails the same way for a deterministic
mismatch. The argument spec prints the refused value in raw output. The assert
is no_log. No effect ran, so nothing is unsafe.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** In lifecycleJudge.result, give a FailedExit with
!j.loaded its own diagnostic: 'the adapter refused its frozen request before
any effect'. Point the remedy at the build. A recorded proved-no-effect
outcome is an optional extension. Consider dropping no_log from request
asserts that read no material.

#### C17-07

**A launch refused by the Go entrypoint (exit 2) or the supervisor guards
(exit 125) ends as the generic failed operation, not as a not-started adapter
with the setup remedy.**

Low · spec gap · both · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/controller_supervisor.py:170`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/controller_supervisor.py:185`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/controller_supervisor.py:197`,
`internal/adapterprotocol/process_linux_amd64.go:29`,
`internal/adapterprotocol/process_linux_amd64.go:308`,
`internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/process_linux_amd64.go:509`

**What:** The Go-owned -c entrypoint
(internal/adapterprotocol/process_linux_amd64.go:29-32) refuses a non-isolated
runtime first and exits 2. The supervisor can then end with exit 125
(controller_supervisor.py:170 and :197; the :170 case also covers a supervisor
that died first, which is deliberate and tested). All of these end as
FailedExit (process_linux_amd64.go:308). They read as 'the adapter operation
did not complete' with the generic remedy
(ansiblerunner/process_linux_amd64.go:509). NotStarted is only the exec
failure (:79). The RuntimeError at :185 is dead defence in depth, because the
entrypoint refuses first. A replaced venv is refused earlier by the venv check
(venvlocal/guard_linux_amd64.go:44). The triggers are near-unreachable.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Map the entrypoint's exit 2 and the supervisor's
exit 125 to the NotStarted diagnostic with setupRemediation in the lifecycle
and controller judges. Keep these statuses reserved so they cannot collide
with playbook exits.

#### C17-08

**No test drives a failing role task's message through the runner to Go's

Low · test gap · both · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:**
`internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/process_linux_amd64_test.go:218`,

**What:** The ansiblerunner test at process_linux_amd64_test.go:218-247 drives

cause. The test at :925 covers refused detail. test_baremetal_replay.py proves
the printed refusal for the five PRINTED_COMPLETIONS. No test asserts that a

The failed-apply golden shows no cause. No cause-carrying behavior exists yet,
so this gap depends on the unimplemented findings C17-01 and C17-02 (the
missing cause on a failed role task). It is not an independent defect.

**Proposed fix (effort M):** Fold into the fix of C17-01 and C17-02: add a
runner-level test that runs a fixture playbook whose task fails with a known
message, then asserts on the diagnostic Go produces and the CLI golden.

### Findings of lane E01

Invocation, privilege, confirmation, authorization and interrupts. Lane
summary: [Lane E01](#lane-e01).

#### E01-03

**A panic in a block goroutine bypasses the internal-error boundary, which
only covers the main goroutine, so direct-root and non-elevated runs get a raw
stack dump and exit 2**

Medium · spec gap · both · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:** `internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/scheduler.go:341`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/scheduler.go:358`,
`cmd/bootwright/internal_error.go:13`

**Scenario:** A capability's evidence check or result handling panics, for
example on a nil map from an unexpected adapter answer. The scheduler starts
each block in its own goroutine (scheduler.go:341) and calls the attempt at
scheduler.go:358 with no recover. The only recover() calls are the
main-goroutine one (cmd/bootwright/internal_error.go:13) and
internal/fanout/fanout.go:139. The Go runtime prints the panic and all stacks
to stderr and exits 2. The block's attempt record stays running, and the
operation is not finalized. A leftover running block is a designed,
recoverable state; only the boundary is missing. It needs a latent bug, so it
is rare.

**What the operator sees:** For direct-root and non-elevated runs: a
multi-screen Go goroutine dump and exit status 2, which the spec reserves for
usage failures. In JSON mode stdout gets no document. Elevated runs get one
structured document, exit 1 and a runtime.internal diagnostic, but the raw
stack still reaches stderr.

**Impact:** This breaks the promise in output.md:1170 that entry points catch
a panic, exit 1 and show a fixed safe summary, and the one-document rule, for
non-elevated and direct-root runs. The panic value can carry authored or
remote text. The result and Next command are lost.

**Recovery today:** Repeat apply or destroy. The running block is resolved by
design.

**Proposed fix (effort M):** Wrap the scheduler's block goroutine, and the
other long-lived goroutines that run capability code, in a recover. Turn a
panic into a step with outcome unknown and a runtime.internal diagnostic
carrying a reference. Reuse the guarded() pattern in internal/fanout
(fanout.go:137-146).

**Already recorded:** Audit 003 finding SEC-02 (an internal-error boundary),
partly delivered by B1133 for the main goroutine only

#### E01-04

**The authorization refusal's "exact command that passes" drops --yes and
every --authorize rebind= the invocation gave, so following it causes a
further refusal**

Medium · output · both · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:** `internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/authorization.go:52`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/authorization.go:83`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/execution.go:106`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/execution.go:113`

**Scenario:** An unattended pipeline runs bootwright destroy --context lab
--authorize rebind=bmc-cred --authorize data-loss --yes. execution.go:106
splits rebind=bmc-cred out before authorized() runs (execution.go:113). The
bare data-loss under --yes refuses, and the remedy is built by invocationFlags
(authorization.go:52, :83-96), which emits only stage, until, authorize tokens
and unregistered. So the remedy command has no --yes and no rebind. Run
without a terminal, it hits the confirmation refusal, whose remedy repeats
every flag and adds --yes. A dropped rebind refuses later, with a remedy that
names the rebind. A dropped --parallelism only resets to the default of 8 and
causes no refusal.

**What the operator sees:** A remedy presented as the command that passes.
Followed literally without a terminal, it refuses once more at confirmation
(requires an interactive terminal), and that refusal's remedy is complete. A
dropped rebind refuses later with its own remedy.

**Impact:** One extra refusal on the unattended path, plus a later refusal if
a rebind was dropped. cli.md:770 promises "the exact command that passes", and
the confirmation remedy does repeat every flag.

**Recovery today:** Follow the confirmation refusal's remedy, which repeats
every flag and adds --yes, or add --yes and the rebind back by hand.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Build the authorization remedy from the
invocation's own arguments, as repeatedCommand does, and rewrite only the
authorize values. Or at least add --yes and the rebinds to invocationFlags.

#### E01-05

**policy trade-off: in a direct root session a second Ctrl-C or SIGTERM is
ignored while cancellation drains; the operator guide's SIGTERM-twice promise
is false there**

Low · spec gap · both · reported as Medium · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:** `cmd/bootwright/interrupts.go:41`,
`internal/controller/privilege/signals_linux_amd64.go:50`,
`internal/controller/privilege/supervised_linux_amd64.go:81`,
`docs/operator-guide.md:715`

**What:** The operator runs bootwright apply from a root SSH login or su -.
The process has no sudo parent, so no supervisor exists and
foregroundOfOwnTerminal returns false. The first Ctrl-C cancels. The privilege
code closes the escalation channel on any second Ctrl-C or SIGTERM, but
interrupts.go:41-44 exits with status 130 only when the process escalates on
its own, and a direct root process does not. The second and later signals are
ignored. A test pins exactly this for an unsupervised binary. cli.md:364-377
covers only the supervisor and the supervised child, so the direct-root case
is not specified.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Either document the direct-root behavior in
cli.md "Local privilege" and in the operator guide, or escalate on the second
signal when the process was not started by sudo. Only sudo can deliver one
interrupt twice.

#### E01-06

**An interrupt landing after the operation is already done prints Done, then
runtime.interrupted and exit 130, as the spec requires; the output contradicts
itself**

Low · output · both · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:** `internal/cli/results.go:60`, `internal/cli/results.go:65`,
`internal/cli/results.go:82`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/attempts.go:715`, `specs/cli.md:784`,
`specs/cli/output.md:31`

**What:** Ctrl-C or an SSH hangup arrives in the short finalize window, after
the last block is done and before the command returns. The operation is
recorded done, so finish returns no next command (attempts.go:715-717).
interruptedLifecycle checks only the cancel cause and that an operation id is
registered, so it is true. writeInterruptedLifecycle prints the Done result
and then runtime.interrupted with an empty remedy.
internal/diagnostics/remediation.go:37 fills in "repeat the command", and the
exit status is 130. An interrupt during a block leaves the operation not done,
so it does not reach this path. The spec requires this output (cli.md:784-786,
output.md:28-35). No test drives the done state.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** When the receipt state is done, write the result
and exit 0, or add a warning that the interrupt arrived after completion. This
needs a spec change in cli.md:784-786 and output.md as well as the code
change. Add a test for the done state.

#### E01-07

**Elevation errors collapse into generic messages ("sudo invocation failed",
"cannot be verified", "cannot be guarded") whose default remedy fits poorly**

Low · output · both · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:** `internal/controller/privilege/elevation.go:52`,
`internal/controller/privilege/elevation.go:136`,
`internal/controller/privilege/elevation.go:288`,
`internal/controller/privilege/process_linux_amd64.go:78`,
`internal/controller/privilege/process_linux_amd64.go:246`

**What:** ProcessExecutor.Run returns the plain error "invocation executable
cannot be verified" when the second ReexecutionPath differs from the first
(process_linux_amd64.go:246-248). A trigger is bin/bootwright rebuilt by make
build in the milliseconds between the two calls. conclude()
(elevation.go:136-137) discards the error and reports "sudo invocation
failed". Executable()'s "invocation executable changed"
(process_linux_amd64.go:78) becomes "invocation executable cannot be verified"
(elevation.go:52-59). Admit (elevation.go:273-288) runs in the elevated child,
not the supervisor. It maps both GuardParent errors to "sudo parent lifetime
cannot be guarded". No test pins the messages.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Carry each executor and guard error as its own
fixed message with a fitting remedy. All are fixed strings with nothing
unbounded. For example: "the Bootwright executable changed while starting;
repeat the command".

### Findings of lane E02

Decision, settling, the operation state machine and re-proof. Lane summary:
[Lane E02](#lane-e02).

#### E02-01

**The state-machine table test decides only the coarse transition and counts
any lifecycle.state refusal as the row's "refuse"**

Low · test gap · both · reported as Medium · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:** `internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/transitions_spec_test.go:452`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/transitions_spec_test.go:470`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/decision.go:213`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/decision.go:221`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/transitions.go:41`

**What:** classify (transitions.go:41) returns one of eight kinds. Guards that
no table row names then decide the visible outcome, such as the
erase-relaxation switch (decision.go:213-220) and refuseUncontinuable
(decision.go:221). decideBy has no case for transitionResolve or
transitionContinue (decision.go:152-211). The test helper decidedAs maps any
lifecycle.state error to "refuse" (transitions_spec_test.go:449-452).
decisionNamed maps every plan without a flag to "continue" (:470). Rows check
only that coarse word, never the error code or the exit command
(checkStateMachine, :360-425). So a row that should refuse with a given exit
passes whichever refusal fires. Refusal messages and exits are individually
pinned by other tests (journey_test.go:4389, finalization_test.go,
lost_records_test.go). Only the tie between a table row and its refusal is
missing.

**Proposed fix (effort M):** Make each guard return a named refusal kind (for
example unindexed, contradicted, uncontinuable, stage, other-build, closure,
host, input-drift, relaxation-differs). Key the table rows and
stateMachineRows cases by that kind and its exit command, not by the string
"refuse".

**Already recorded:** none. The knowledge page
reconciliation-audit-2026-10.md:72 already notes that the test "drives decide
only", but no open item tracks it.

#### E02-03

**The moved-basis refusal tells the operator to repeat the bare verb, so a
staged or bounded apply is told to run a plain apply that plans every stage**

Medium · output · both · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:** `internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/reproof.go:147`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/authorization.go:83`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/commands.go:18`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/operation_plan.go:67`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/registration.go:164`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/registration.go:484`

**Scenario:** An operator runs `bootwright apply --context c --stage
substrates` (or --until) to stop at a boundary. While the prompt waits,
another invocation finalizes or advances the context. At the exclusive
re-proof, the check at reproof.go:147 builds its remedy with
contextCommand(context, verb), which has no flags. All eight callers pass only
the verb, and the recorded basis (operation_plan.go:67) holds no selection.
invocationFlags (authorization.go:83) and planCommand (commands.go:18) exist
but are not used. Following the remedy runs a plain apply, a wider plan with
no later refusal; with --yes it runs every stage. A destroy with erase or
data-loss steps is still refused without its --authorize tokens, and that
refusal names the full command. A preparation operation is told to run bare
apply; admitPreparationCommand (decision.go:172) refuses it and names the
right command, one extra step.

**What the operator sees:** lifecycle.state 'the context changed after this
command read it: it was planned from operation X (running), and the context
now holds operation X (unknown) with different block states', with remedy
'repeat bootwright apply --context c to plan from what the context holds now'.

**Impact:** Medium. The remedy names a command with a different meaning from
the one refused. For apply with --stage or --until, following it widens the
plan, and an --yes script or a hurried operator runs every stage.
Re-presentation and confirmation still stand in the way for other cases.

**Recovery today:** Re-type the original flags by hand.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Carry the invocation's selection (stage or until)
into the basis, and build the remedy with planCommand and invocationFlags. Or
name the original command line in the refusal.

#### E02-05

**policy trade-off: once an update changes a completed apply's input, destroy
is the only way on, even after the original bytes are restored**

Medium · dead end · apply · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:** `internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/decision.go:292`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/decision.go:296`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/decision.go:342`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/decision.go:377`

**Scenario:** An apply completes. The operator runs `context update` with an
edit, even a comment (the input digest hashes raw bytes), and accepts past the
warning. Then they reimport the original files. Each import makes a new
revision. settleApply calls inputDrift (decision.go:292), and the case at
decision.go:342 returns a revision drift whenever the apply's revision differs
from the selected one. settleApply then refuses with changedInput
(decision.go:296), and namedChange words it (decision.go:377). The
keep-revision rule applies only when the manifest equals the selected
revision, so a restoring update does not help. The spec states this behavior
(contexts.md:207-211, state-reconciliation.md:40-44).

**What the operator sees:** 'the desired state changed after this apply
completed: its input revision changed, though its bytes repeat the ones this
apply froze', with remedy 'take back what it owns with bootwright destroy ...,
then run bootwright apply ...'.

**Impact:** Medium. The whole platform must be torn down to undo an input
edit. The refusal and the warning (shown before the prompt,
contexts.md:200-211) are clear, but the exit is out of proportion.

**Recovery today:** Run `bootwright destroy`, then `bootwright apply`. No way
to select or roll back to an older revision exists in the spec.

**Proposed fix (effort M):** B598: settle over a revision whose bytes equal
the frozen digest. The existing detection of repeated bytes at decision.go:377
already finds this case.

**Already recorded:** B598 (open). Decision D155, the owner's earlier choice
to accept this case, deferred the fix to a future slice (backlog.md:1724,
:4915). The spec already documents the behavior.

#### E02-07

Low · output · both · verified: combined narrowed

because the context update guard refuses an input change that would invalidate
exact continuation (specs/contexts.md, Frozen input and provenance). The state
is reachable only through store damage or a restored backup. The tests reach

command selects an earlier revision, since a re-import makes a new one
(contexts.md:208-211). For an incomplete apply that can be superseded, destroy
never checks input (verifyRemovalHost, reproof.go:171, does not call
recordedRefusal), so it is the working exit.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Name the supersede (takeBackUnder) when
supersedable(operation) is true, and otherwise name the backup restore.

**Already recorded:** none. The open item B598 concerns completed applies, so
it is a different case.

#### E02-08

**Vague refusal after an incomplete finalization: it names no operation and no
lagging item, though the spec requires the refusal and a repeat usually
works**

Low · output · both · verified: combined narrowed

under a shared lock and finds another finalization due
(finalization.go:131-138). The code refuses with lifecycle.state and says to
repeat the verb. The spec (specs/state-reconciliation.md, lifecycle unit
paragraph) requires this refusal rather than repeating. The realistic cause is

then repeating is the right remedy. A permanent loop needs a store that keeps

(finalization_test.go:752-770, which pins the wording).

finalization mark still finds lagging (evidence not its projection,
reservation held).

#### E02-10

(preparation.go:182). The sibling branch at preparation.go:180 uses

### Findings of lane E03

Registration, mutation evidence, claims, reservations and Secret binding
holds. Lane summary: [Lane E03](#lane-e03).

#### E03-01

**After a registration stops once it has reserved, status shows a clean idle
context and context update refuses with a wording that cites an operation that
does not exist**

Low · output · apply · reported as Medium · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:** `internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/registration.go:291`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/registration.go:435`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/status.go:245`,
`internal/workspace/contexts/refusals.go:52`

**What:** A first apply on context lab reaches register(). The controller
binding is published and host reservations are published. Then the
registration stops before the index write: a plan.json or operation.json write
error, the size bound on admission, a Ctrl-C inside the transaction, or a kill
or power cut after the reserve. restoreEvidence() sees no index entry and a
held reservation, returns nil at registration.go:291 and keeps the running
evidence. This is required by specs/state-reconciliation.md:259-263. Status
takes the no-index branch (status.go:241-246). unindexed() deliberately
accepts running apply evidence (registration.go:435), so status shows no
contradiction and offers plan and apply. The pending-evidence guard then makes
context update refuse with the incomplete-operation message (refusals.go:52),
although no operation exists to continue.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Name this state in status, beside the
no-operation line, with the held reservations and running evidence. Make the
context update refusal tell 'pending evidence with no index entry' apart from
a real incomplete operation, and name apply or destroy as the release.

#### E03-02

**A Secret held by an unnamed binding over a completed apply gets the remedy
'destroy', when a plain apply would finalize the context and lift the hold**

Medium · output · both · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:** `internal/secrets/custody/holds.go:91`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/secret_holds.go:38`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/finalization.go:41`

**Scenario:** Context lab holds a completed apply. The operator runs an
additive apply. It raises running evidence and binds new Secret material. The
process is killed in the window between raising and registering. (Controlled
failures restore the applied evidence, so a kill is the trigger.) The index
still names the done apply, the evidence reads running, and an orphan binding
pins current Secret versions. Then `bootwright secret generate --renew --name
X` hits a Secret that binding pins. secret_holds.go:38 sets Registering. The
binding is unnamed, so the refusal says an apply still registering may name
it, and the remedy at holds.go:91 says destroy only. An apply would run
finalization first (finalization.go:41), republish applied evidence and lift
the hold.

**What the operator sees:** 'Secret X's current version is held by the Secret
binding \<id>, which an apply still registering may name, and no command
reveals a bound version; nothing was written', with the remedy 'take the
context back with bootwright destroy --context lab, which releases the
binding, then repeat the command'.

**Impact:** The remedy points at destroy, when `bootwright apply --context
lab` would clear the hold. Destroy is not run blindly: it needs a plan and
confirmation, and it finalizes first, then decides again. The operator can
still be steered toward removing a completed platform to renew one Secret. The
state needs a kill in a short window, so it is rare.

**Recovery today:** Run `bootwright apply --context lab`. It takes the
finalization path, republishes applied evidence and lifts the hold. Then
repeat the Secret command. Nothing in the message tells the operator this.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** When the hold comes from Registering and the
index names a completed apply, make the remedy text name `bootwright apply
--context \<ctx>`. Keep destroy for real effect-material holds. The spec
(secrets.md:448-453) states no remedy for this case, so this is a text change,
not a spec conflict. Optionally limit Registering so paused applies and
destroys with an orphan unnamed binding stop saying 'apply still registering'.

#### E03-03

**A failed preparation-addition registration keeps its added host reservations
under applied evidence until the preparation is repeated or the context is
destroyed**

Low · loose end · apply · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:** `internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/register_run.go:202`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/registration.go:291`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/preparation.go:269`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/additive.go:104`

**What:** Context lab holds a completed apply. A preparation addition
(Prepare, or an apply with a preparation scope) runs register() with
reserveAddition true. reserve() calls tx.Reserve, which publishes the old and
new host-keyed reservations durably, and nothing rolls them back. Then
store.Register fails before the index write, a rare write failure.
restoreEvidence() keeps evidence only for a Destroy/Done index with a held
reservation (registration.go:291), so over a completed apply it settles
applied evidence and leaves the new keys. retainReservations
(register_run.go:201-202) keeps them on later additive reserves. Add-on
additive applies are not affected: they reserve nothing
(specs/state-reconciliation.md:159-205). The spec is silent on this
restoration.

**Proposed fix (effort M):** When a preparation-addition registration provably
did not happen, restore the context's reservations to the set the current
operation reserved, inside the restoration transaction, or reserve additions
only in the transaction that writes the index.

#### E03-04

**No test asserts the status text, next steps or update and delete refusal
wording over running evidence with a reservation and no index entry**

Low · test gap · apply · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:** `internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/registration_test.go:391`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/status.go:240`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/kill_harness_test.go:1086`

**What:** TestAFailedRegistrationWithReservationsKeepsItsEvidence
(registration_test.go:391) asserts only the running evidence, the
reservations, the released binding and the destroy recovery. It never calls
Status. Status over no index with running evidence goes through unindexed(),
which accepts running evidence (registration.go:425-440), and returns
idleSteps (status.go:240-247, 354-363). No lifecycle test asserts that text.
kill_harness_test.go:1086 runs Status at every kill point but asserts only
that it does not error. The running-evidence refusal that context update and
delete share is tested generically in
internal/reconciliation/contextguard/disposition_test.go. The additive crash
test (additive_journey_test.go:218) checks that no reservations are held.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Extend the existing registration tests: after the
failure, assert the status text and next steps, and the update and delete
refusal wording over running evidence with a reservation and no index. For a
preparation addition, also assert the controller record's reservations.

### Findings of lane E04

Planning, stages, the pause boundary, additive apply and lineage. Lane
summary: [Lane E04](#lane-e04).

#### E04-01

**Plan-size refusals name the kind of limit but not the count, and point to a
status remedy that cannot help**

Low · output · apply · reported as Medium · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:** `internal/reconciliation/plan.go:104`,
`internal/reconciliation/plan.go:543`, `internal/reconciliation/plan.go:279`,
`internal/reconciliation/state.go:179`,
`internal/diagnostics/remediation.go:74`

**What:** An Environment is large enough that its plan goes over a bound. The
block limit is 256 blocks, so a plan like the 61-block, 6-node lab case needs
roughly 25 or more nodes to reach it. The operator runs plan or apply. NewPlan
refuses with a failure under the lifecycle.state code (planError at
state.go:179, nothing wraps it). The same path covers a block request over 256
KiB and the 4 MiB aggregate. Nothing is registered. The remedy falls back to
the generic lifecycle.state default, which is to run status. A separate,
internal case is an unresolved requirement (plan.go:279). It names its target
but not the block that needs it. That one is a planner defect, not operator
input.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Add the numbers to the message (for example 'the
plan holds 271 blocks; a plan holds at most 256'). Name the block ID and
object where one is responsible. Give the refusal a remedy that says to split
the Environment into contexts or reduce Machines. Keep lifecycle.state for
durable-state conditions and give plan-shape refusals their own code.

#### E04-02

**The required refusal to add an instance where gitops is the last package
uses a generic message that omits the cause and offers only destroy**

Medium · output · apply · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:** `internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/additive.go:142`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/additive.go:308`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/stage_tails.go:31`,
`internal/addons/instance/capability.go:118`,
`internal/reconciliation/delta.go:45`

**Scenario:** A completed apply has an OpenShift cluster whose add-on bindings
include gitops, the last package (packages/gitops.go:15 sets Last). The
operator adds a binding member, updates the context, then applies. The
additive path plans the new instance. dependOnStageTails
(stage_tails.go:31-45) makes every block that is last in its stage wait for
each same-stage block that needs the cluster, so the gitops block now depends
on the new instance. Compare marks that block Changed (delta.go:45).
additive.go:142-145 refuses. Durable state is unchanged, but the input is
already updated. The refusal is required by the spec
(state-reconciliation.md:180-183) and listed as a limitation
(delivered.md:10607). The same text appears when the last package is the one
being added to an existing instance.

**What the operator sees:** lifecycle.state: this executable would freeze the
block \<addon-...-gitops> differently from the plan this apply froze, so the
input is no addition to it; remedy: take back what it owns with bootwright
destroy --context \<ctx>, then run bootwright apply --context \<ctx>; bootwright
diff --context \<ctx> shows each change

**Impact:** The refusal itself is deliberate. The defect is the message and
the remedy. It never says why: the existing gitops instance would have to wait
for the added one. The only remedy given is destroying the whole platform. The
operator may suspect build drift and retry.

**Recovery today:** bootwright destroy --context \<ctx>, then bootwright apply
--context \<ctx> with the full set of packages.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** When the changed block differs only by waiting on
added blocks, say so in plain words: the existing instance \<x> would wait for
the added \<y> (gitops runs last on \<cluster>), so it cannot be added after the
apply. Tell a Changed block apart from a Removed one. The test
additive_journey_test.go:246-262 pins only the generic fragments.

**Already recorded:** none (B598 concerns restoring old input, not this
message)

#### E04-03

**policy trade-off: a failed add-on addition, or a failed add-on in an
incomplete apply, can only be dropped by destroying the whole lineage**

Medium · dead end · both · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:** `internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/reproof.go:186`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/lineage_removal.go:41`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/additive.go:106`,
`specs/state-reconciliation.md:204`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py:308`,
`internal/addons/instance/capability.go:120`

**Scenario:** An additive apply is registered over a completed platform
(additive.go:106 needs a finished predecessor), and its add-on block fails,
for example an operator subscription that cannot resolve in the catalog. The
failed addition is now an incomplete head. Changing its input hits
recordedRefusal (reproof.go:186). Destroy plans the whole lineage: every
earlier plan is folded into one removal (lineage_removal.go:41-49). The spec
states no removal takes back an additive apply alone
(state-reconciliation.md:204-206, 1956-1958). A second lane reported the same
dead end in a fresh incomplete apply: a pinned add-on version missing from the
catalog fails the block, a repeat fails the same way, and a corrected pin is
refused as changed input. Another lane reported that case at medium
confidence.

**What the operator sees:** On a changed input: lifecycle.state: the context
input changed after this operation registered; restore the exact input
revision this operation froze. This does not name destroy. The operator guide
(operator-guide.md:866-869) and the destroy plan (warning tested in
lineage_removal_test.go:452) disclose the whole-lineage removal. A repeated
apply fails the same way.

**Impact:** A failed add-on forces a choice between a context stuck in a
failed state and rebuilding the whole platform, including its data. The
trigger is uncommon. It is deliberate policy, rated Medium.

**Recovery today:** Fix the external cause and run bootwright apply again, or
run bootwright destroy and then apply with the corrected binding. Destroy
takes back every Machine, cluster and storage block of the lineage.

**Proposed fix (effort L):** Allow removing an additive head whose added
blocks provably had no effect, so the earlier plan becomes current again. Or
revive B769 (online instance removal) and extend its revive condition to heads
with effects. For the incomplete-apply case, let the operator finish the apply
without failed add-on instances, then add the corrected one.

**Also reported as:** C15-07

**Already recorded:** B769 (parked, backlog.md:2398) covers only per-instance
online removal, not head-only removal of a failed addition. Audit 004 REC-63
(report-fable.md:500, 7111) only discloses this and recommended extending
B769's revive condition.

#### E04-04

**An unreadable or uncompilable frozen revision makes additive apply fall back

Low · output · apply · verified: combined narrowed

`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/decision.go:359`

**What:** A completed apply was registered by an earlier build. The operator

**state-reconciliation.md says 128 impacts and 8 exclusive resources per

### Findings of lane E05

Scheduler and executor. Lane summary: [Lane E05](#lane-e05).

#### E05-01

**An additive apply that fails after registering but before its receipt is set
releases the root apply's frozen Secret binding, so a later destroy refuses**

High · unsafe · apply · verified: combined narrowed, reach narrowed

**Where:** `internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/executor.go:56`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/executor.go:90-92`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/executor.go:196`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/executor.go:212`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/attempts.go:714`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/register_run.go:66`

**Scenario:** A root apply that consumed Secrets holds binding B0. An additive
apply (for example, adding an add-on instance) is decided fresh and lists B0
as held. Registration publishes the new operation with only its own binding
B1, and the outcome becomes registered. Then run() returns a result with an
empty receipt, because the operation-log open (executor.go:196), the
block-state read (executor.go:212) or a step of finish before attempts.go:714
fails. The receipt is set only at attempts.go:714, so the kept list stays
empty (executor.go:56). Collect still runs (executor.go:90-92) and releases
B0, with no guard (registration.go:351-356). Triggers: an in-process I/O error
in the short window after registration. An interrupt landing just after
registration also works, because the block-state read uses the live context
and the operation area refuses a cancelled one
(operations_linux_amd64.go:313). A crash or SIGKILL does not, because collect
never runs. A full disk probably also fails the release, so nothing is lost
then. Later, destroy reopens the root's first binding (lineage_removal.go:48)
and refuses as a lost binding (frozenbinding.go:109-112).

**What the operator sees:** First the apply's runtime.log or store failure, or
the interrupt. Later, every destroy of the lineage refuses with a
lifecycle.state error naming a lost binding. The remedy offered is to restore
the context's keyring from a complete backup and repeat, or to run context
delete and remove the named objects by hand.

**Impact:** Bootwright can no longer remove the lineage by itself. The frozen
Secret material of the root apply is gone, though no operation chose to
release it. The trigger is a short window, but the loss is permanent. Both
verifiers rated it Medium on the I/O trigger alone; the orchestrator's
re-check found the interrupt trigger and keeps it High.

**Recovery today:** Restore the context's keyring from a complete backup and
repeat the destroy. Or run context delete --purge --allow-orphans, which the
lost-binding remedy offers, and remove the objects it names by hand.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Compute the kept list from the registered
operation ID, which is known once register returns, instead of from the
receipt. Or skip collect unless finish completed. Add an additive-apply test
that fails the operation-log open after registration and asserts the root
binding is not released.

**Orchestrator re-check:** Both verifier lenses confirmed the mechanism and
rated it Medium, because they found only an I/O fault as trigger. The
orchestrator re-read the code and found a second trigger: the block-state read
that follows registration (internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/executor.go:212)
uses the invocation's live context, and the operation area refuses a cancelled
context before anything else
(internal/workspace/contextfs/operations_linux_amd64.go:313), so an interrupt
that lands just after an additive apply registers also returns a result
without a receipt and releases the predecessor's binding. An interrupted run
is a realistic path and the consequence is permanent (the lineage's frozen
Secret material is gone), so the finding stays High. The window is short, tens
of milliseconds after registration.

#### E05-02

**policy trade-off: a required-log fault cancels every in-flight sibling
block, so healthy blocks end unknown; the spec requires this**

Low · unsafe · both · reported as Medium · verified: combined narrowed, reach
narrowed

**Where:** `internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/logging.go:40`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/executor.go:190-192`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/removal_gates.go:104-106`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/attempts.go:114-116`,
`internal/reconciliation/state.go:96`,
`specs/state-reconciliation.md:1620-1622`

**What:** Several blocks run together. One block's required attempt log cannot
be written, for example the log disk is full, or a quota or I/O error hits.
logging.go:40-43 latches the fault and calls the cancel of the shared work
context (executor.go:190-192 for apply, removal_gates.go:104-106 for destroy).
Each in-flight sibling is told to stop and returns Canceled whatever it had
finished. attempts.go:114-116 records that as canceled, and state.go:96 turns
canceled into unknown. The operation ends unknown. This is deliberate: the
spec requires cancellation on a log fault, and a test pins it. The trigger is
uncommon. The one cascade on record came from a race that is now fixed
(.agents/knowledge/concurrent-block-execution.md:50-54).

**Proposed fix (effort M):** Change the spec first, because it requires
cancellation. Then, for a fault confined to one block's log, let in-flight
siblings finish under a non-cancelled context and mark only the faulted block
unknown. Draining helps little when the log root is the same disk as the state
store, since siblings then cannot record either.

#### E05-05

**A failed run prints a generic default 'Next' for each block cause that

Low · output · both · verified: combined narrowed
