`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/removal_gates.go:242`

**Scenario:** Uncommon topology: one context runs Ceph on owned virtual
Machines, and a cluster in the same context consumes it from retained or
physical Machines. Plan warns in advance with lifecycle.surviving-consumer. On
destroy, the code finds the consumer's Machines are not all deleted by the
same destroy, so the consumer is a survivor. The quiescence proof
(proveQuiescent) refuses first, before any host probe, using only the frozen
plan, so every repeat gives the same refusal. The spec requires this refusal
until online Ceph removal exists. The remedy text (const at :253, used at
:277) states a design rule, not an action. Minor, rare second point: if the
frozen request cannot be decoded (:192-199, :243-246), the same "consumes ...
and survives" text is shown, blaming a running consumer.

**What the operator sees:** error lifecycle.live: this removal would take back
state that is still in use: \<consumer kind>/\<x> consumes \<provider kind>/\<y>
and survives this destroy, which takes back \<provider kind>/\<y>. Remedy: keep
this context while the consumer runs; a destroy takes back what a consumer
uses only when the consumer leaves with owned virtual node Machines the same
destroy deletes

**Impact:** The refusal is deliberate, but the context cannot be destroyed by
any Bootwright destroy, and the remedy gives no way out. The consumer is in
the same plan, so no command removes it first. The trigger is uncommon and
warned at plan time. Medium.

**Recovery today:** `context delete --purge --allow-orphans`, then tear down
both clusters by hand. Nothing in the message names this. Online Ceph removal
(B491) would let the destroy pass.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Change the remedy to name `context delete --name
\<name> --purge --allow-orphans` and say it abandons both clusters, which then
need manual teardown. Give a read error its own text, such as "the frozen
request of \<consumer> cannot be read". The refusal itself stays until B491.

**Also reported as:** X15-04

**Already recorded:** B491 (online Ceph removal) and D183 (the owner decision
to refuse until B491) track the refusal itself; the remedy wording and the
read-error wording are untracked

#### E08-07

**A removal refused because the superseded operation records no block it still
owns gives fixed text that names neither the operation nor the
contradiction.**

Low · output · destroy · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:** `internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/removal_plan.go:28`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/decision.go:539`

**What:** An apply ended failed or in an unknown state, and its owned block
records read empty because the records were lost. The code at
decision.go:538-541 skips the contradiction check when the owned subset is
empty and the apply is not a started-nothing apply. The removal then refuses
at removal_plan.go:26-29 with a fixed sentence. That sentence names no
operation id and none of the contradictions. The fuller contradiction wording
at contradictions.go:65-66 is not used here. The spec sentence at
specs/state-reconciliation.md:1736-1738 requires the refusal to name the apply
and each contradiction. Reaching this state needs store damage (lost block
records).

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Reuse the contradictions() text and include the
operation id and state in this refusal. Name the contradiction that the state
says a block started but none is recorded. Update the test at
lost_records_test.go:457 that pins the current text.

#### E08-08

**At the online and pre-stop boundaries, the removal refusal prints a
placeholder data-loss digest although the removal is registered and its plan
digest is fixed.**

Low · output · destroy · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:** `internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/removal_gates.go:293`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/commands.go:70`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/online_gates.go:44`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/online_gates.go:76`

**What:** proveQuiescent is called at the online and pre-stop boundaries
(online_gates.go:44,76). At these points the removal is registered and its
plan is the frozen plan, so the digest is fixed. The refusal at
removal_gates.go:293 still builds its repeat command with
authorizingUnfixed(plan), which prints a placeholder (commands.go:70,80). The
paused continuation command (commands.go:110-122) prints the real digest from
authorizing(frozen), so the refusal and status disagree. The same may hold at
scheduler.go:388 if that removal is shown to be registered. Before
registration (executor.go:179, removal_gates.go:84) the placeholder is
deliberate. There the remedy re-decides a fresh removal after resolution has
changed block states, and specs/cli.md:278-283 allows it. Tests pin that case.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** On the boundary path only, pass authorizing(plan)
so the registered removal's real digest is printed. Leave the placeholder
before registration. specs/cli.md:281 asks for the digest where the code holds
the plan.

### Findings of lane E09

Operation store, record encoding and the private log writer. Lane summary:
[Lane E09](#lane-e09).

#### E09-03

**Index, plan, block and attempt record refusals carry no remedy, so the
default 'run status' loops back to the same refusal; the index refusal also
misses its spec remedy**

Medium · dead end · both · verified: combined narrowed, arbiter narrowed

**Where:** `internal/reconciliation/operationstore/records.go:267`,
`internal/reconciliation/operationstore/records.go:272`,
`internal/reconciliation/operationstore/records.go:286`,
`internal/reconciliation/operationstore/records.go:314`,
`internal/reconciliation/operationstore/records.go:324`,
`internal/reconciliation/operationstore/records.go:574`

**Scenario:** The record has no usable build member. That covers the index,
the plan, block state records, an operation record that fails validation
(version unsupported, records.go:324), and an attempt record that names the
running executable but does not decode (records.go:267). The trigger is a
later-build or foreign or hand-edited index, or a shape change limited to the
plan or a block record. A shape change to the operation record refuses first
with a proper remedy. No build writes another index version. decodeUnder and
validateIndex return recordError with an empty remedy. The CLI then fills in
its default, 'run bootwright status ...'. status reads the same index first
and refuses the same way.

**What the operator sees:** `lifecycle.state: lifecycle record is malformed or
unsupported` (or 'lifecycle index version is unsupported' or 'lifecycle record
is not canonical'), with no path, operation id or block id. The remedy says
'run bootwright status --context \<context> to see the records and the next
step'. Running status prints the same refusal.

**Impact:** A remedy loop with no named exit, on every apply, destroy and
status. The spec says an index of another version refuses with a remedy naming
the build that prepared it, then context delete --purge
(state-reconciliation.md:445-448). The code names neither. The spec sentence
about not sending the operator to status covers operation records only, so
only the index clause is unmet.

**Recovery today:** bootwright context delete --name \<ctx> --purge
--allow-orphans, which no message names. Or the earlier build that wrote the
store, or a backup restore, if the operator guesses it.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Send every decode or validate refusal of the
index, block, attempt and plan records through one helper, as
operationDecodeError does for operations. Name the record path and the build
when known. Never use the status default; always name the purge exit. Add the
'this executable' arm. Audit 004 (REC-88) proposes dropping the spec clause,
so the fix is in code or spec.

**Also reported as:** E02-04, O06-02

**Already recorded:** Index-version half only: audit003:RCC-04 (rated Low,
audits/003-code/report-final.md:1913). The plan, block and operation-version
loop is untracked.

#### E09-04

**The frozen-plan rebuild refusal after a build update tells the operator to
read operation.json for the build instead of naming it, and offers only
destroy**

Medium · output · both · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:** `internal/reconciliation/operationstore/store.go:713`,
`internal/reconciliation/operationstore/store.go:725`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/decision.go:107`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/status.go:100`

**Scenario:** A failed or paused apply exists. The operator installs a newer
build whose NewPlan structural rules differ. ReadPlan rebuilds the plan, finds
a different digest and refuses with a fixed remedy. It does this before it
reads the operation record that holds the registering build. apply, destroy
and status all return this error unchanged, so status fails the same way and
no Bootwright command names the build. The spec lets the other build continue
an operation it froze, but the remedy names only destroy.

**What the operator sees:** `lifecycle.state: the frozen plan is not a plan
this executable could have produced`, with the remedy 'destroy this context
with the build that registered the operation, which its operation.json
records'. That file is root-owned under /var/lib/bootwright.

**Impact:** The operator needs root and knowledge of the file layout to learn
which build to reinstall. The trigger is a build update that changes plan
rules: uncommon but realistic. Medium.

**Recovery today:** sudo cat
contexts/\<name>/state/operations/\<op>/operation.json, install the build it
names, then continue or destroy with that build.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Name the build in the message, using
BuildIdentity(operation.Executable) from the operation record the callers
already read, or have ReadPlan read the operation record first. Offer
'continue or remove it with that build, or delete the context'.

#### E09-05

**A cancel that lands after the running-block record is renamed, past its
after-checkpoint, reports 'published lifecycle record is unsafe' instead of
the interrupt**

Low · output · both · reported as Medium · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:** `internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/attempts.go:73`,
`internal/reconciliation/operationstore/store.go:1029`,
`internal/workspace/contextfs/publication_linux_amd64.go:79`,
`internal/workspace/contextfs/publication_linux_amd64.go:93`

**What:** Ctrl-C, or the log-fault latch's cancel(), arrives while the start
of an attempt is publishing the running-block record. attempts.go:73 hands the
cancellable context to StartAttempt, and store.go:1029 publishes the record.
The message 'published lifecycle record is unsafe' appears only if the cancel
lands after the after-checkpoint has passed: inside the read-back, during or
after the directory sync, or in the final read-back
(publication_linux_amd64.go:79-93). A cancel before that checkpoint gives a
raw 'context canceled' instead. The window is very narrow, from microseconds
to one fsync. The one recorded occurrence came from a file-exists race that
has since been fixed.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Run the store writes of StartAttempt and
RecordPreparation under recordingContext, as the completion writes already do,
and check cancellation only before the write starts. Or have publishStage map
a post-rename context error to an explicit 'interrupted after publication'
outcome.

#### E09-09

**A run killed after dropping log events leaves no dropped-event marker, and a
reopened full operation log gains one marker per run until the area refuses
it**

Low · spec gap · both · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:** `internal/reconciliation/operationstore/logs.go:304`,
`internal/reconciliation/operationstore/logs.go:335`,
`internal/workspace/contextfs/operations_linux_amd64.go:704`

**What:** (a) A run is killed after Log.Append has dropped events. The marker
is written only at Close, so none is written. This breaks the output spec's
rule that truncation and dropped-event counts are explicit
(specs/cli/output.md:1292). It applies to attempt logs too (128 KiB bound), so
it is the more reachable half. (b) The operation log (8 MiB) is full. Each
reopen drops 'opened', and Close appends one more marker with no limit check
(logs.go:335). Append reserves only 64 bytes (logs.go:304). After several
repeat runs the area refuses it at operations_linux_amd64.go:704, and the log
fault latches again on every later run. Only the reopened operation log is
affected, because attempt logs are new per attempt.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Count the marker against the limit and write at
most one per file. Have OpenLog treat a log at its limit as proven without
appending. Write the marker as soon as the first drop happens, not at Close.

### Findings of lane E10

Ansible runner, adapter result protocol and process supervision. Lane summary:
[Lane E10](#lane-e10).

#### E10-02

**A failed adapter run carries no exit status or signal, so an unreachable
host or a kill reads as any other failure and needs the root-only output
file**

Low · output · both · reported as Medium · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:** `internal/adapterprotocol/process_linux_amd64.go:308`,
`internal/adapterprotocol/run.go:90`,
`internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/process_linux_amd64.go:509-510`,
`internal/controller/venvlocal/guard_linux_amd64.go:44`,
`internal/adapterprotocol/process_linux_amd64.go:31`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/controller_supervisor.py:196-197`

**What:** The adapter ends with a non-zero exit or a signal. Two realistic
cases: the playbook child is OOM-killed, or ansible-playbook exits 4 because
the target host was unreachable. In both, reaped() ends the session as
FailedExit with no failure (process_linux_amd64.go:308). FailedExit carries no
data (run.go:90), so the exit code and signal are dropped. The runner then
returns one fixed text, 'the adapter operation did not complete'
(ansiblerunner process_linux_amd64.go:509-510). The silent cases the finder
listed (entrypoint exit 2, supervisor exit 125) are not reachable in practice.
The venv guard checks the runtime before every launch
(guard_linux_amd64.go:44), so those two exits are only backup checks.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Carry the exit status and signal in the failed
ending. Show them in the message, with a clear wording for a signal death and
for exit 4 (unreachable target). Always log the exit status in the attempt
log.

#### E10-04

**A protocol breach (invalid or incomplete result) gives a fixed sentence with
no reason, and the offending record is logged nowhere; the trigger is an
internal build defect**

Low · output · both · reported as Medium · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:** `internal/adapterprotocol/process_linux_amd64.go:319-321`,
`internal/adapterprotocol/process_linux_amd64.go:332-333`,
`internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/process_linux_amd64.go:389-433`,
`internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/process_linux_amd64.go:407-409`,
`internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/process_linux_amd64.go:511-514`

**What:** This needs an internal build defect: the collection and the Go
decoder ship in one embedded bundle, so a mismatch between them is not a state
an operator can reach. Example defects are a role emitting an undeclared group
id, or a record the decoder rejects. Judge returns Valid=false with no reason
(ansiblerunner:389-433), and the runner ends Invalid with no failure
(adapterprotocol:332-333). On a decode error, readEnded keeps only Incomplete
and drops the decoder error (:319-321). The runner maps both to fixed
sentences (ansiblerunner:511-514). Only group records are logged
(ansiblerunner:407-409), so the offending record appears nowhere. The spec
fixes the effect of a breach but not its message.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Return a closed reason from Judge and keep the
decoder's error kind. Put both in the message, and log a protocol event with
that reason.

#### E10-06

**A canceled or timed-out Ceph block leaves its remote worker running for up
to 640 s, and the runner comment at line 314 claims more than that**

Medium · unsafe · both · verified: combined narrowed, reach narrowed

**Where:** `internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/process_linux_amd64.go:314`,
`ansible/ansible.cfg:30`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/ceph_native_worker.py:1-9`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/ceph_native_worker.py:43`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/ceph_native_worker.py:44`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/ceph_native_worker.py:273`

**Scenario:** During a Ceph block the operator presses Ctrl-C, the run
deadline fires, or the link drops. The local supervisor ends the local process
tree, including the ssh clients. The remote worker started its own session
(setsid). It ends its group only on HUP, TERM or INT. A lost ssh channel that
delivers no signal is bounded only by the worker's total time limit: 640 s, or
1920 s for the package worker. The attempt is recorded as canceled or unknown,
and the engine resolves or retries the block meanwhile. The worker's own
comment says it does not claim to stop on disconnect.

**What the operator sees:** A canceled block or an unknown outcome. If a
second bootstrap starts inside the window, a misleading partial-cluster
refusal or a failed block. Nothing tells the operator that a remote worker may
still be running.

**Impact:** No confirmed damage. A second bootstrap is blocked by the
bootstrap-attempt.json marker. What remains is a misleading refusal or failed
block during the window. Later Ceph phases assume they can safely run twice,
and nobody has checked that under concurrent runs.

**Recovery today:** Wait out the window (up to 640 s, or 1920 s for the
package or bootstrap worker), then repeat apply. No printed message tells the
operator to wait.

**Proposed fix (effort M):** As B573 proposes: end remote workers when the
channel closes, or make the resolution wait out a remote limit. Reword the
runner comment to say it covers only the local tree. Add a spec clause that
states the remote window, for example near specs/security.md:320. No spec
sentence claims remote workers die, so none needs correcting.

**Also reported as:** X08-04

**Already recorded:** B573 (open, specs/milestones/backlog.md:141 and
:1488-1515)

#### E10-08

**The leftover-descendants refusal names the job lock path but not the
processes that still hold it**

Low · output · both · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:** `internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/jobs_linux_amd64.go:238`,
`internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/jobs_linux_amd64.go:236-239`,
`internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/jobs_linux_amd64.go:200-203`

**What:** Bootwright is killed, and a descendant process survives the
supervisor's tree kill, for example a module stuck in uninterruptible sleep.
It still holds the adapter job lock, although the kernel freed the holder
lock. The next apply or destroy of the context runs sweep
(jobs_linux_amd64.go:200-203). heldRefusal's default arm (:236-239) then
refuses, naming the lock path but no process ID or command. This is a safe,
fail-closed state. The text is pinned by a test
(jobs_linux_amd64_test.go:209).

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Scan /proc/*/fd for the lock file and name the
process IDs and their commands in the message.

#### E10-09

**If Ctrl-C or the deadline lands after a valid refusal but before the adapter
is reaped, the named refusal is replaced by 'interrupted' or an unknown
result**

Low · output · both · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:** `internal/adapterprotocol/process_linux_amd64.go:383`,
`internal/adapterprotocol/process_linux_amd64.go:333-336`,
`internal/adapterprotocol/process_linux_amd64.go:346-350`,
`internal/adapterprotocol/process_linux_amd64.go:238-242`,
`internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/process_linux_amd64.go:495-496`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/attempts.go:114-115`

**What:** The adapter writes a valid refused record. The runner records a
named ending (process_linux_amd64.go:333-336), closes the input and kills
nothing (:346-350), as the spec says, so the playbook goes on to its cleanup
tasks. The window lasts only until the adapter is reaped. If Ctrl-C or the
deadline lands inside it, cancel() sets the canceled flag (:238-242).
outcome() checks `case s.canceled:` (:383) before the recorded ending, so the
refusal is dropped. The runner maps canceled to the context error
(ansiblerunner:495-496), and the attempt is recorded as canceled, not failed
(attempts.go:114-115). No test covers cancel after a refusal. The spec is
silent on which wins.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** In outcome(), prefer an already recorded named
ending over canceled, or show the refusal as a diagnostic beside the
cancellation.

#### E10-10

**Several pre-launch failures share the lifecycle.state code and one text with
an empty remedy, so a full /run cannot be told from a build defect**

Low · output · both · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:** `internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/process_linux_amd64.go:273`,
`internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/process_linux_amd64.go:293`,
`internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/process_linux_amd64.go:296`,
`internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/jobs_linux_amd64.go:139`,
`internal/diagnostics/remediation.go:74`,
`internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/process_linux_amd64.go:190-202`

**What:** A JSON encoding error, a write error under /run (for example a full
tmpfs) and a failed record rename all return 'the frozen adapter invocation
could not be materialized' with an empty remedy (process_linux_amd64.go:273,
293, 296; jobs_linux_amd64.go:139). No file or error class is named. The 4 MiB
size bound the finder listed is designed to be unreachable (a test bounds a
request below it), so a write error such as a full /run is the real trigger.
Many other lifecycle.state sites also carry no remedy, including
request-invariant refusals (process_linux_amd64.go:190-202, runner.go:42-45,
outputs_linux_amd64.go:30-35). One code for all of these is the spec's choice.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Name the file and the error class on I/O errors,
so a full /run is recognizable.

### Findings of lane E11

Context store, locks, lease, transactions and the deletion guard. Lane
summary: [Lane E11](#lane-e11).

#### E11-01

**A busy context lease or root lock names no holder, and status probes no
process, so a stopped or hung holder cannot be told from a working one**

Low · output · both · reported as Medium · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:** `internal/workspace/contextfs/kernel/locks_linux_amd64.go:20`,
`internal/workspace/contextfs/kernel/locks_linux_amd64.go:33`,
`internal/workspace/contextfs/kernel/locks_linux_amd64.go:49`,
`internal/workspace/contextfs/repository_linux_amd64.go:1146`,
`internal/workspace/contextfs/files_linux_amd64.go:516`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/status_live.go:12`

**What:** One terminal runs `bootwright apply --context lab-libvirt`. The
process is suspended (Ctrl-Z or a tmux suspend, an uncommon trigger) or hangs
inside a long effect. In another terminal, `status` shows the operation as
running, because status probes no process (stated spec policy at
output.md:1057). A second `apply` takes the lease through leaseContext, and
the non-blocking flock fails. The code returns Busy with "context state is
held by another mutator". A holder of the host-wide root lock gets a different
text, "context storage is busy" (files_linux_amd64.go:516 is the root-lock
wait). The same refusal also covers a bounded run such as machine power.
Nothing records the holder's pid, command or operation. A dead holder releases
the lock, so a refusal proves a live process.

**Proposed fix (effort M):** Write a small holder record (pid, start time,
verb, operation id) beside the lease when it is taken. On a busy refusal, read
it and name the holder, the lock kind and whether the pid is alive or stopped.
Optionally let status run the same non-blocking lease test that `logs
--follow` already runs.

**Also reported as:** X05-01

#### E11-03

**policy trade-off: damage to one context's directory makes every context
refuse, and the only named exit is a whole-store restore that no command or
tested procedure provides**

Medium · dead end · both · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:** `internal/workspace/contextfs/repository_linux_amd64.go:580`,
`internal/workspace/contextfs/repository_linux_amd64.go:658`,
`internal/workspace/contextfs/repository_linux_amd64.go:929`,
`internal/workspace/contextfs/repository_linux_amd64.go:1461`

**Scenario:** Context A's directory is replaced (for example restored from an
rsync or tar backup), or its reservation file is damaged. Every read, and
every write transaction, proves the mappings of all ready contexts. So apply,
destroy and status of healthy context B also refuse with 'context A cannot be
verified: contexts/A: context directory was replaced', and the remedy is
'restore the whole store from a matching backup'. A matching backup must keep
every inode, meaning a whole-root image taken with no lock held
(specs/contexts.md:912-920). No command takes or restores one. Copying the
whole store with cp -a to a new disk would damage every context, not only A.
The spec itself calls this remedy 'not a supported exit' until B103 lands
(B103 is the open item for an explicit complete-store restore).

**What the operator sees:** A context.state refusal that names context A while
running a command for context B, with only the 'restore the whole store from a
matching backup' remedy.

**Impact:** A file-level restore or a store move, the ordinary way to back up
or move a directory, makes the whole controller unusable for every context,
including destroying B's live objects. The spec states this openly
(specs/contexts.md:416-436, 903-920). It is a recorded dead end, not a
surprise, but no operator procedure exists. Medium.

**Recovery today:** Restore a whole-store image that kept every inode (the
operator's own act). Or, once no owned object remains anywhere, run controller
uninstall --discard-unreadable.

**Proposed fix (effort L):** Real fix is B325 (isolate a damaged context so
the others keep working, and let purge or abandon with --allow-orphans accept
a replaced directory) and B103 (explicit complete-store restore). Stopgap:
document a tested whole-store backup procedure and add one test that restores
such an image.

**Already recorded:** B325 (backlog.md:630, names the destroy-blocked case),
B103 (backlog.md:27, :434)

#### E11-04

**policy trade-off: an orphan-acknowledged context delete lists no abandoned
objects; it points at status and diff, which stop working after the delete,
and --yes shows no plan**

Medium · output · destroy · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:** `internal/workspace/contexts/service.go:672`,
`internal/workspace/contexts/service.go:690`,
`internal/cli/output_contexts.go:130-145`,
`internal/cli/output_context_plan.go:91`,
`internal/workspace/contexts/requests.go:85-98`,
`internal/cli/testdata/context-delete-plan.golden:9`

**Scenario:** Destroy of context lab-libvirt keeps failing on an unreachable
host, so the operator runs `bootwright context delete --name lab-libvirt
--purge --allow-orphans --yes`. Service.Delete skips confirmDeletion when
SkipConfirmation is set (service.go:672), so no plan is shown. The result
built at service.go:690 carries only Name, OrphansAbandoned and
ReleasedReservations. Without --yes the plan lists work areas and freed keys
(output_context_plan.go:67-71), but for owned objects it only says that
`bootwright status` and `bootwright diff` list them (:91-93). DeletionPlan
holds no object list. After the delete both commands refuse, because the
context no longer exists. This follows specs/contexts.md:935-941 and :983-995.
Under --yes the operator chose to skip the plan.

**What the operator sees:** Warning `context.orphaned: the objects this
context owned were abandoned and are no longer managed`, then `Context
deleted`, `Orphans abandoned true`, `Reservations released: ...`.

**Impact:** The operator is not told what was abandoned on which host
(domains, disks, networks, services, installer work areas, Ceph keys), and
nothing can tell them afterwards. A later init of the same name adopts them
(B568). Medium.

**Recovery today:** Run status and diff before the delete and keep their
output. After it, only manual inspection of each host, for example by
context-name prefix.

**Proposed fix (effort M):** Have the delete compute the abandoned inventory
itself (kind, object and host, from the operation records it already reads).
Show it in the plan, in the result including under --yes, and in the
structured output.

**Also reported as:** X17-07, X09-08

**Already recorded:** B324 (backlog.md:62, :624; open, parked). B578 covers
only the status inventory.

#### E11-05

**A flock error other than contention, or a failed evidence read, is reported
as another mutator or a concurrent change, and the kernel error is dropped**

Low · output · both · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:** `internal/workspace/contextfs/files_linux_amd64.go:506`,
`internal/workspace/contextfs/kernel/locks_linux_amd64.go:34`,
`internal/workspace/contextfs/kernel/locks_linux_amd64.go:51`,
`internal/workspace/contextfs/reconciliation_linux_amd64.go:371`,
`internal/workspace/contextfs/reconciliation_linux_amd64.go:388`,
`internal/diagnostics/remediation.go:45`

**What:** awaitRoot and kernel.Lock (and the shared lock at locks:51) map
every flock error other than EWOULDBLOCK to `context.state` "context state is
held by another mutator". A non-blocking flock cannot return EINTR, so the
real triggers are ENOLCK or EBADF. In PublishEvidence, a failed read of
state/mutation.json (EIO, or the file missing) is reported as "context
mutation evidence changed before publication". That discards readBounded's own
specific refusals and the open errno. contextfs already has storeCauseText
(files_linux_amd64.go:64) for this. The "changed" wording is right when the
file reads fine but differs.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Carry the errno with storeCauseText: say "the
kernel refused the lock on \<state root>: \<errno>" for the lock, and the read's
own refusal for the read. Keep the "changed" wording only when the bytes were
read and differ.

**Also reported as:** X05-08

#### E11-06

**A failed unlink in the context deletion walk names neither the entry nor the
kernel error, after the context is already marked Deleting**

Low · output · destroy · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:** `internal/workspace/contextfs/deletion_linux_amd64.go:231`,
`internal/workspace/contextfs/deletion_linux_amd64.go:293`,
`internal/workspace/contextfs/deletion_linux_amd64.go:437`,
`internal/workspace/contextfs/deletion_linux_amd64.go:450`,
`internal/workspace/contextfs/deletion_linux_amd64.go:682`

**What:** `context delete --purge` passes the inspection walk.
removeContextDirectory then marks the registry record Deleting and drops the
controller claims (:437-448), and only then runs the removal walk (:450).
Unlinking one file fails, for example EPERM from an immutable attribute set by
a backup or security tool, or EROFS or EIO. unlinkMatching (:293-296) discards
the errno and returns "context deletion target could not be removed".
deletionDamage (:682-692) rewraps only unverified entries, so this plain error
passes through with no entry name and no errno.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** At the walk's call site (:231), wrap the failure
with unverifiedEntryRefusal(dir, name, ..., errno text) so deletionDamage
names the entry, the errno and the manual exit. Do not change unlinkMatching
itself: about 20 other callers use it where deletionDamage does not run.

#### E11-07

**A non-private file in a removed context's log directory leaves it Deleting,
and the refusal names the file but calls it a directory and omits restoring
mode 0600**

Low · output · destroy · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:** `internal/workspace/contextfs/logs_linux_amd64.go:66`,
`internal/workspace/contextfs/logs_linux_amd64.go:314`,
`internal/workspace/contextfs/logs_linux_amd64.go:325`,
`internal/workspace/contextfs/logs_linux_amd64.go:357`,
`internal/workspace/contextfs/deletion_linux_amd64.go:353`,
`internal/workspace/contextfs/deletion_linux_amd64.go:450`

**What:** An operator ran `sudo chmod 644` on an attempt-NNNNNN.output file to
read it without sudo. A later `context delete --purge` removes the store tree
first (deletion:450-459). Then removeContextLogs (:353) reaches removeLogTree,
whose default branch (logs:314-315) finds the 0644 file and returns
unsafeLogPath(\<file path>). That text says "the log directory \<path> is not a
private directory" and "remove \<path> or replace it with such a directory".
Nothing saves the registry, so the context stays Deleting. The unlink failures
at :325 and :357 are the other exits from the same walk. The refusal itself is
required by log-root.md:126-131.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Use file wording for a file entry, naming mode
0600 or the extra link as the cause and the exit. Optionally, drop the
registry entry even when only the log subtree is left, and report the leftover
path. That second part is a design choice, not a defect.

### Findings of lane E12

Secrets during a lifecycle run: bindings, keyring, custody and lent material.
Lane summary: [Lane E12](#lane-e12).

#### E12-01

**policy trade-off: any keyring-wide corrupt-store error is read as a lost
binding, and the message names no entry, so the operator cannot find the stray
file or missing part**

Low · output · both · reported as Medium · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:** `internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/frozenbinding.go:71`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/frozenbinding.go:110`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/frozenbinding.go:246`,
`internal/secrets/localkeyring/artifacts.go:60`,
`internal/secrets/localkeyring/artifacts.go:117`,
`internal/secrets/localkeyring/localkeyring.go:122`

**What:** An apply is failed or paused and holds a Secret binding whose own
material is intact. Then the keyring gets a problem outside that binding: an
unsupported file appears under the context's secrets state directory, or the
part file of an unrelated Secret version is lost (for example disk loss or an
interrupted copy). Every keyring session open runs a whole-keyring check,
which returns secret.store.corrupt for the entire keyring. On apply or destroy
the lifecycle cannot list the binding, so it reopens it, sees the corrupt
code, and declares the binding lost. Status adds the lost-binding
contradiction and offers only the context deletion as next step. The specs
require corrupt to read as lost.

**Proposed fix (effort M):** Keep corrupt-equals-lost for the binding's own
versions. Report a keyring-wide check failure (an extra file, or a missing
part of a version the binding does not pin) with its own code that names the
entry relative to the state root and says to remove it and repeat. Optionally
have Reopen check only the artifacts the binding needs.

**Already recorded:** none (B364 and B374 are adjacent: they cover other
listing failures, not this one)

#### E12-02

**policy trade-off: after a completed removal, a keyring that stays unusable
loops on 'repeat destroy', and plain context delete refuses because evidence
is not pristine**

Low · dead end · destroy · reported as Medium · verified: combined narrowed,
arbiter narrowed

**Where:** `internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/finalization.go:242`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/finalization.go:278`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/finalization.go:281`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/attempts.go:697`,
`internal/reconciliation/contextguard/guard.go:31`,
`internal/workspace/contexts/refusals.go:122`

**What:** A destroy has every block recorded done. The keyring then becomes
unusable and stays so (missing key file, a whole-keyring check failure, or a
ledger fault). The code writes the operation done, then withdraw
(attempts.go:697) or the binding Release (finalization.go:242) fails. The
pristine evidence is published only after those releases, so it is never
published. The message says to repeat destroy to finish it, and every repeat
fails the same way. Plain context delete refuses because the guard accepts
only pristine evidence, and it says the context still owns realized objects.
The repeat wording is required by the spec and tested for a transient error.
The trigger is uncommon: the keyring must break after the last block and stay
broken.

**Proposed fix (effort M):** Give the guard its own disposition, with no
--allow-orphans needed, for a done removal whose only remaining debt is
keyring releases or the withdrawal. Make the terminal remedy stop asking for a
plain repeat while the cause persists.

**Also reported as:** X15-03

**Already recorded:** none (B374, at backlog.md:709-711, is adjacent: status
offers verbs that refuse on key-unavailable)

#### E12-03

**Keyring key-unavailable and seal-limit errors name no file, Secret or
binding, and their default remedies do not fit the local keyring**

Low · output · both · reported as Medium · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:** `internal/secrets/secretstore/values.go:148`,
`internal/secrets/localkeyring/localkeyring.go:252`,
`internal/secrets/localkeyring/mutations.go:549`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/frozenbinding.go:50`,
`internal/diagnostics/remediation.go:56`,
`internal/diagnostics/remediation.go:60`

**What:** A lifecycle verb opens the keyring and the key file keys/\<id>.key is
missing or not 32 bytes. The keyring returns secret.store.key-unavailable,
'secret encryption key is missing or unsafe', with no object and an empty
remedy. On a fresh apply the raw error comes back. On a frozen binding the
listing fails too, so the cause is also returned as it failed. The default
remedy then says to make the Secret store key or unlock session available, but
the local keyring has no unlock session and the key can only return from a
backup. The seal limit (about one million seals per key) has the same gap: its
default remedy says to reduce the Secret material, where the fitting exit is
secret encryption rotate. That limit is rare in an apply.

**Proposed fix (effort M):** Give key and ledger failures an object, the
context-relative artifact path. Give each its own remedy: key missing means
restore keys/ from a complete backup; seal exhaustion means secret encryption
rotate. In the lifecycle, attribute a reopen failure to the binding and
operation it served, as the lost-binding message already does.

**Already recorded:** B374 (status side only)

#### E12-04

**secret delete drops the current version of a live effect-material binding,
because only set, generate and renew are guarded by holds**

Medium · spec gap · both · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:** `internal/secrets/custody/service.go:524`,
`internal/secrets/custody/service.go:594`,
`internal/secrets/custody/holds.go:76`, `specs/secrets.md:425`

**Scenario:** An applied context has a binding that pins effect material at
its current version, such as a disk recovery passphrase or a delivered fleet
key. The operator runs `bootwright secret delete --context <ctx> --name
\<secret>`. Delete (service.go:524-555) and deleteConfirmed
(service.go:560-595) never call readHolds or refuseHeld. The path ends at
deleteCurrent (service.go:594), which drops the current mapping. The bound
version is kept, because a binding references it. `secret list` then shows the
Secret as orphaned with a bound version, and no command reveals that version.
Also, holder() (holds.go:76-78) treats a name with no current version as not
held. So a later `secret set` or generate is not refused and creates a new
version beside the bound one.

**What the operator sees:** A normal delete confirmation and success. Nothing
says that the only copy the operator can read, of material a live effect still
uses, is now unreadable. `secret list` shows the Secret as orphaned with a
bound version.

**Impact:** The hold rule says the current version is the only copy the
operator can read, and that nothing may replace it. Delete breaks this. A
host's disk passphrase or an SSH key still planted on running hosts can no
longer be revealed through Bootwright while the effect lives on. Apply and
destroy keep working, because the bound version is retained. The loss is the
operator's reveal path.

**Recovery today:** None through Bootwright. The bound version is reopened
only by lifecycle attempts. A backup restore brings it back.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Apply refuseHeld in Delete and deleteConfirmed
under the lease, with the same secret.store.conflict refusal and remedy as
set. Or decide in the spec that delete is allowed, say so in the delete
confirmation, and amend the spec's hold section (specs/secrets.md:425-434) and
its retention note (specs/secrets.md:152) either way.

**Already recorded:** none (B372 covers only delete's confirm-and-revalidate)

#### E12-05

**A Bind that committed but returned an error leaves a binding the executor
never releases, and the operator sees the secret store's own cleanup remedy
during apply**

Low · loose end · apply · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:** `internal/secrets/localkeyring/mutations.go:448`,
`internal/secrets/localkeyring/metadata.go:79`,
`internal/secrets/localkeyring/localkeyring.go:371`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/executor.go:96`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/registration.go:251`

**What:** A fresh apply calls Bind. The selector publish commits, then cleanup
fails (collectArtifacts, mutations.go:446-448) or the publish returns
Committed or Uncertain with an error (localkeyring.go:371-387). Bind returns
the error and no binding identity, so the executor's bind() returns an empty
identity. The failed-registration path then has nothing to release
(registration.go:251-256). The committed binding is named by no operation. The
spec states this orphan and says the next fresh registration, removal
finalization or destroy collects it (specs/secrets.md:353-358). A failed
release there is also left silently on purpose, and the code comment says so.
The trigger is a filesystem fault after the commit.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Optional polish: have Bind return the committed
binding identity with a cleanup warning so the caller can release it, and let
the apply message also say that repeating apply collects the orphan.

### Findings of lane E13

The controller stage: prerequisites, runtime, bundle, host binding and client
tools. Lane summary: [Lane E13](#lane-e13).

#### E13-01

**In a removal, a lost controller tool area gives the remedy "apply --stage
controller", which the incomplete destroy itself refuses**

Low · dead end · destroy · reported as Medium · verified: combined narrowed,
arbiter narrowed

**Where:** `internal/controller/prerequisites/tools.go:60`,
`internal/controller/prerequisites/tools.go:71`,
`internal/controller/prerequisites/service.go:286`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/attempts.go:548`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/attempts.go:567`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/transitions.go:57`

**What:** A context's apply finished its controller stage, then failed later.
The operator runs destroy, which starts a removal. A removal block that needs
`oc` or `kubectl` looks the tool up. The lookup code (attempts.go:567-616)
does not check whether it runs in a removal. If the controller area or its
retained sources were lost outside Bootwright, the lookup fails at
tools.go:71-73 and names "run bootwright apply --stage controller --context
\<name>" (service.go:286-290). The apply refuses over an incomplete destroy
(transitions.go:57-58, decision.go:182-184). The code at attempts.go:548-553
says a removal must not name apply, so it contradicts its own intent. The
missing-bundle remedy (tools.go:61, 64-65) names apply the same way. The
trigger is narrow. Areas stay bound until context delete, controller uninstall
refuses while a context exists, and a build change mid-destroy is refused
early. A tool layout change without a tag move is hypothetical.

**Proposed fix (effort M):** Make the lookup refusal depend on the verb. In a
removal, name a remedy that can act, such as re-publishing the retained
closure during removal, or the registering build. Amend
specs/controller.md:820-822. Hashing the tool layout into the stage's
content-digest pin is separate hardening.

#### E13-02

**Controller-adapter refusals not on the named-refusal list leave no cause in
the output, so a lasting cause fails every retry the same way.**

Medium · output · apply · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/controller_refusal.py:17`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/controller_refusal.py:35`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/action/controller_tool.py:76`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/controller_files.py:766`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/controller_files.py:782`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/controller_files.py:857`

**Scenario:** During `apply --stage controller`, after the continue
acknowledgement was delivered, the controller tool step raises a plain refusal
whose name is not in the known list. Examples are "bundle ownership", "bundle
replaced", "bundle file changed", "publication bounds" and the proxy refusals;
about 30 sites raise such refusals. The record function returns nothing for
them, and the warning at controller_refusal.py:35 fires only for the
acquisition kind. The task message is a fixed text and the task is hidden
(no_log). Go sees a plain failed exit and shows the generic text. Because the
acknowledgement was delivered, the attempt state is unknown. The triggers are
rare, for example a wrong-owner area or a replaced bundle directory.

**What the operator sees:** controller.install "Ansible did not complete the
authorized dependency operation" with "Preserve the controller state and
restore the qualified controller execution environment, then run bootwright
apply --stage controller --context \<name>." The root-owned attempt output does
not hold the refusal name either.

**Impact:** The cause is recorded nowhere, not even in the private output. A
lasting cause, such as an area owned by the wrong user or a replaced bundle
directory, fails every retry the same way. Only reading the source can
diagnose it. Rare triggers, so Medium.

**Recovery today:** None from the output. The operator must guess or read the
source. The delivered note says raw lines reach the private output, but that
holds only for classified refusals.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Write the refusal name (a closed, bounded token)
or its detail to the Ansible warning for every refusal, as is already done for
the acquisition kind. Optionally add a closed `bundle` class (and `request`)
that Go maps to a message naming the tool area path.

#### E13-03

**The scratch-space and private-storage failures of the Ansible adapter give
the generic environment-integrity correction and name no path or byte
counts.**

Medium · output · apply · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:** `internal/controller/ansiblelocal/runner_linux_amd64.go:384`,
`internal/controller/ansiblelocal/runner_linux_amd64.go:110`,
`internal/controller/ansiblelocal/runner_linux_amd64.go:115`,
`internal/controller/ansiblelocal/installer.go:190`

**Scenario:** A context selects openshift-clients and the installer (hundreds
of MB) and /var/tmp is small. The capacity check at runner_linux_amd64.go:384
finds too little free space and fails. The same shared failure helper
(installer.go:189-190) gives every adapter failure one correction, "Preserve
the controller state and restore the qualified controller execution
environment", and the stage step appends "then run bootwright apply --stage
controller --context \<name>." The "private Ansible invocation storage is
unavailable" (/run) and "private Ansible staging storage is unavailable"
(/var/tmp) failures at :110 and :115 get the same text. These are
operator-fixable, not protocol breaks. The other adapter failures are true
protocol breaks and rightly keep it.

**What the operator sees:** "the staging filesystem has too little free space
for the approved dependency payloads", with no path (/var/tmp), no required or
available byte counts, and a remedy about restoring the execution environment.

**Impact:** Operator-fixable conditions (disk space, unavailable /var/tmp or
/run) are shown as an environment-integrity problem. The operator cannot tell
which filesystem is short or by how much.

**Recovery today:** Guess /var/tmp, free space, and run `bootwright apply
--stage controller --context \<name>` again.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Give each of these three failures its own
correction. Name /var/tmp or /run, and for capacity give the required and
available bytes. Keep the generic correction for true protocol breaks.

#### E13-04

**The controller stage's dnf install and removal deadlines are reported as a
dnf configuration error instead of a timeout**

Low · output · apply · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:** `internal/controller/hostdnf/packages_linux_amd64.go:237`,
`internal/controller/hostdnf/packages_linux_amd64.go:243`,
`internal/controller/hostdnf/packages_linux_amd64.go:246`,
`internal/controller/hostdnf/removal_linux_amd64.go:151`,
`internal/controller/prerequisites/service.go:214`

**What:** The controller stage installs the hypervisor packages from a slow
Satellite. Packages.Install runs under a 1-hour deadline
(prerequisites.InstallDeadline, service.go:214). When it expires, dnf is
killed and the run returns -1 with an error. The code only checks the parent
context (:243), which is not done, so it falls to `err != nil || exit != 0`
(:245-246). The message carries the last line dnf printed, often a download
progress line. The attempt is marked unknown. Preview handles its own deadline
(:205-207), so the asymmetry is real. Packages.Remove
(removal_linux_amd64.go:151-164, "dnf did not complete the removal") has the
same gap, while its Preview handles the deadline (:127-129).

**Proposed fix (effort S):** In both Install and Remove, check the install or
removal context's error as Preview does. Report that dnf did not finish within
the deadline, with a correction about repository reachability.

#### E13-05

**A certificate refusal from an artifact mirror with a lent trust anchor names
only the system trust store, not the declared anchor Secret**

Low · output · apply · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:** `internal/controller/prerequisites/refusals.go:20`,
`internal/controller/ansiblelocal/runner_linux_amd64.go:273`,
`internal/controller/ansiblelocal/runner_linux_amd64.go:296`,
`internal/controller/ansiblelocal/installer.go:165`,
`internal/controller/bundlelocal/mirror.go:157`

**What:** An Environment declares an artifact mirror with trustBundleRef. The
Secret holds a CA that does not issue the mirror's current certificate, for
example after rotation. The Python adapter's TLS check fails and classifies
the failure as "certificate" (controller_files.py:106-107). It verified
against the system roots plus the lent anchor (controller_files.py:281-286,
425-433), and neither accepted. The runner calls AdapterRefusal with only the
host (runner_linux_amd64.go:273). The request's trust host is available
(installer.go:165) but unused. The message names only the system store. The
bundle path names both for the same cause (bundlelocal/mirror.go:157), so the
wording differs for one cause. A handshake failure is "certificate", not
"trust anchor", which applies only at context load.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** When the refused host equals the request's mirror
trust host, use a condition and correction that name both the system trust
store and the Secret in trustBundleRef, as bundlelocal/mirror.go:157 already
does. The no-anchor wording stays, as tests pin it.

#### E13-06

**policy trade-off: a runtime-guard failure in the controller stage names
"apply --stage controller" while other blocks name "controller install"**

Low · output · both · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:** `internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/attempts.go:105`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/attempts.go:553`,
`internal/controller/venvlocal/adapter.go:89`,
`internal/controller/venvlocal/guard_linux_amd64.go:41`,
`internal/controller/prerequisites/remedies.go:35`,
`internal/controller/prerequisites/remedies.go:44`

**What:** A host change breaks the controller's Python runtime, so the runtime
guard (verifyRuntime) fails. These failures carry no command of their own
(guard_linux_amd64.go:41, 94-135). An ordinary block reads "..., then rerun
bootwright controller install" (remedies.go:35). The controller-stage apply
block is wrapped by stageReading with InStage (attempts.go:105, 553-557),
which gives "..., then run bootwright apply --stage controller --context
\<name>." Only setup's Build retires and rebuilds a runtime that fails
verifyRuntime (build_linux_amd64.go:76-95). The stage apply rebuilds only an
unpublished runtime (lifecycle/runtime.go:226-235), so the named command can
refuse again. Spec controller.md:853-857 requires the stage command, so this
is a spec rule applied too widely to the runtime guard. The trigger is rare.
The unprepared-runtime case deliberately keeps "Run bootwright controller
install" in its correction.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Make the venvlocal correction name controller
install, as the unprepared-runtime case does, or exclude guard-entry failures
from stageReading. Giving the failure a command does not work, because InStage
discards a failure's own command (remedies.go:44-49).

### Findings of lane E14

Composition root: capability binding and error translation for reconciliation.
Lane summary: [Lane E14](#lane-e14).

#### E14-01

**policy trade-off: an unexpected untyped error ends as runtime.internal with
fixed wording, with no cause shown and no cause in the attempt log**

Low · output · both · reported as Medium · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:** `internal/cli/runner.go:336`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/scheduler.go:458-473`

**What:** Apply or destroy gets a plain Go error that no boundary turned into
a diagnostic. Examples are a store read error a contextfs adapter left
unwrapped, or a capability that returns fmt.Errorf. Runner.outcome checks
interruption, ErrNotImplemented, Canceled, DeadlineExceeded and
diagnostics.Of, finds none, and falls to the last line. Inside a block,
scheduler.reported does the same and says the block stopped on a failure that
escaped a typed boundary. The fixed wording is owned by
specs/state-reconciliation.md:881, which says runtime.internal names the block
and is never in the failure's own words. specs/cli/output.md:1170 defines the
code as an unexpected failure that escaped a typed boundary. Capabilities are
meant to return typed diagnostics, and contextfs already maps the common
storage errnos (files_linux_amd64.go:44-54). So this is an unexpected escape,
not a routine failure class.

**Proposed fix (effort M):** Add a short error class (for example errno,
timeout or permission) to the runtime.internal message, plus a reference id.
Write the raw cause to the private attempt log under that id. This does not
weaken secrecy.

#### E14-02

**A corrupt embedded runtime lock in a broken build is reported as 'bootwright
apply is not implemented' instead of as a build defect**

Low · output · both · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:** `cmd/bootwright/wiring_controller.go:67`,
`cmd/bootwright/wiring.go:136`, `cmd/bootwright/wiring_reconciliation.go:389`,
`cmd/bootwright/wiring_reconciliation.go:417`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/service.go:84-95`,
`internal/cli/runner.go:306`

**What:** Only a broken build reaches this: runtimelock.Embedded() returns an
error because the embedded runtime lock is corrupt. The lock is go:embed
(internal/controller/runtimelock/embed.go:14), and
cmd/bootwright/controller_wiring_test.go:34 and embed_test.go parse it, so a
tested build does not hit it. localControllerDependencies drops the error and
leaves Python nil (wiring_controller.go:67). runtimeGuard(nil) returns nil, so
wireLifecycle returns lifecycle.Service{} (line 389). Apply and destroy then
get availability.ErrNotImplemented from service.go:84-95, and runner.go:306
renders cli.not-implemented with the help remedy. Other missing fields are not
reachable, since production always wires Workspace and Host
(wiring.go:134-136).

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Keep the wiring error (embedded lock decode,
missing port) and surface it as a runtime.build diagnostic naming the missing
port. Reserve ErrNotImplemented for deliberate stubs (wiring_stubs.go).

**Already recorded:** audit005:G05-06 (audit 005 already records this defect,
with the same Embedded() site and fix)

### Findings of lane G01

Plan-time, freeze-time and thaw-time refusals of the capability requests. Lane
summary: [Lane G01](#lane-g01).

#### G01-01

**Bound-Secret refusals at attempt time give a remedy that cannot work: SMB
and agent-install messages say to repeat apply, and the Ceph key message
implies a rebind the spec forbids**

Medium · dead end · apply · verified: combined narrowed, arbiter narrowed

**Where:** `internal/storage/ceph/host_trust.go:87`,
`internal/storage/ceph/host.go:583`,
`internal/storage/ceph/smb_materials.go:22`,
`internal/containercluster/agentinstall/capability.go:317`,
`internal/storage/ceph/requests.go:727`

**Scenario:** A FIPS CephCluster has an imported (not generated) cluster SSH
key Secret holding an ssh-ed25519 key. Planning checks only
source.generated.keyType (requests.go:727-731), so the key passes and the
cluster binds that Secret version. At run time boundMaterial (materials.go:58)
and host.go:583 call proveClusterKey, which refuses at host_trust.go:87, and
the block fails. A continuing apply presents the version its operation bound.
The cluster key is effect material, and effect material refuses rebind
(specs/secrets.md:404-410). So a repeated apply reads the same Ed25519 version
and refuses again. The SMB message says 'then apply again' and the
agent-install message says 'repeat the apply'. Both name that loop. The Ceph
message names no command but implies a rebind. No one verified that the SMB
password has no admission check on this path.

**What the operator sees:** The Ceph block shows [FAIL] with 'FIPS Ceph
refuses the bound cluster SSH key' and 'bind an ECDSA or RSA cluster SSH key'.
The SMB message ends with 'then apply again' (smb_materials.go:22). The
agent-install message says 'repeat the apply' (capability.go:317). Following
any of them gives the same refusal.

**Impact:** The operator is sent into a loop on a remedy that cannot work. The
real exit, destroy then replace the Secret then apply, is not named by any of
the three messages. The trigger is uncommon, so Medium.

**Recovery today:** Run bootwright destroy --context \<ctx>, replace the
Secret, then run bootwright apply. None of the three messages says so.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Use the wording installation/key_policy.go:53-55
already uses: take the context back with bootwright destroy --context \<ctx>,
replace the Secret, then run bootwright apply, since a continuing apply reads
the bound key version. Name the CephCluster in the Ceph message. Separately,
check the key type at registration, before the first effect.

**Already recorded:** none. B1175 only moves the agent-install Ed25519 refusal
to admission, so it partly overlaps but does not fix the remedy text.

#### G01-02

**policy trade-off: the controller-prerequisites package table sits outside
the contract digest and commit contract list, so a table-only change refuses
late**

Low · dead end · both · reported as Medium · verified: combined narrowed,
arbiter narrowed

**Where:** `internal/controller/clients/requests.go:177`,
`internal/controller/clients/requests.go:203`,
`internal/controller/clients/capability.go:196`,
`internal/controller/clients/capability.go:208`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/other_build.go:21`,
`scripts/check-commits:22`

**What:** A context was applied, or left failed, by build A. Destroy with
build B reads the controller-prerequisites block. Removal calls DecodeRequest,
which compares the frozen package list with B's package table and refuses. The
block's Destroy only publishes retained evidence. The spec chooses this: a
removal proves its execution contract, and the operator removes effects with
the build that created them. The three cited commits (89d4e074c, e0940ce15,
51bc3c447) each moved the contract by hand, so the contract check refused
first. A table-only change has never happened. The real gap is that
internal/controller/prerequisites/ is not in check-commits contract_paths and
the digest pins a tag, not the table, so such a change could land with no
Contract line and refuse late.

**Proposed fix (effort M):** Add internal/controller/prerequisites/ to
check-commits contract_paths, or fold the package table into the contract
digest, so a table change must declare its contract. Do not exempt the removal
from contract equality: that contradicts the spec and needs an owner spec
change.

**Already recorded:** none found; the BREAKING CHANGE footers record it as
deliberate

#### G01-03

**Dependency-proof refusals name no Machine, profile or disk and reuse one
sentence for several causes; they are defensive checks with no realistic
trigger**

Low · output · both · reported as Medium · verified: combined narrowed

**Where:** `internal/managedos/installation/dependency_proof.go:16`,
`internal/managedos/installation/dependency_proof.go:37`,
`internal/managedos/installation/package_tree_proof.go:32`,
`internal/storage/ceph/disk_proof.go:38`,
`internal/managedos/diskdiscovery/inventory.go:57`,
`internal/managedos/diskdiscovery/inventory.go:66`

**What:** A Ceph host block's attempt asks for the proof of its dependency's
installation. When no unique completed record matches the Machine and its
frozen address, the code refuses. That one sentence covers a duplicate record,
a record not done, an address mismatch, a proof this build cannot re-validate,
and an invalid key. Five of the six refusals have an empty remedy, so the
generic 'run bootwright status' is added. None names the Machine, though the
function receives it. The ProveRoot closure covers about a dozen refusal sites
(inventory.go:66-129); discovered_root.go:19 repeats the same text. The disk
proof names neither host nor path. These are integrity checks on proofs from
the original apply. The scheduler starts a dependent block only after its
dependency is done, so a missing or duplicate proof needs store corruption or
a lineage bug. Failing closed is deliberate. No realistic trigger was found.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Put the Machine, profile, disk path and cause in
each message (not unique, not done, address mismatch, proof invalid, absent),
and attach the object identity. Replace 'restore the original apply records'
with the real exits, as lostBinding does. Use a distinct sub-code per cause.

#### G01-04

**The post-discovery refinement gate refuses with one fixed message that names
no object or field, and inventory-read failures reach the same refusal**

Medium · output · apply · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:** `internal/managedos/diskdiscovery/preparation.go:129`,
`internal/managedos/diskdiscovery/preparation.go:158`,
`preparation.go:254`

**Scenario:** The operator runs bootwright machine discover, then edits the
input: selects a root disk and also adds an object or changes another field.
bootwright apply goes through the preparation decider and then the refinement
gate. The gate refuses with one fixed message when the object count changes,
when an object is missing from the earlier set, and when any object changes
while an installation is owned. The loop holds current.Kind() and
current.Name() but never reports them. An inventory or claims read failure
also becomes the same refusal, because one || condition at about line 158
sends every error to refused(). The specific causes from refinementInventory
are discarded. The earlier owned-block check at about line 233 does name the
block, so the gap is edits that leave owned blocks unchanged. This happens at
plan time.

**What the operator sees:** 'only root-discovery policy and unowned
storage-device refinements may follow preparation' with 'keep prepared
ownership unchanged and update only the disk-selection fields'.

**Impact:** The operator has to diff the input by hand to find the offending
edit. A legitimate data-disk refinement refused because the inventory read
failed looks like an illegal edit. The state stays recoverable, so Medium.

**Recovery today:** Revert edits until the refusal stops. bootwright diff may
help.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Name the object (Kind/Name) and the first
differing field, or say 'object added/removed'. Report an inventory or claims
read failure in its own words instead of through refused().

the other sites do not name the Machine.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Classify the plan-again sites as internal

#### G01-08

**Dependency-proof contract refusal at evidence.go:207 names the block but not

**What:** The spec says an implementation-contract refusal names its block and

Small roles and helper utilities the first round did not cite. Lane summary:

#### G02-01

**Every failure of the console administrator credential prepare or update
becomes one generic failure, so the specific refusals the spec promises are
never shown**

Medium · output · both · verified: combined confirmed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/modules/containercluster_admin_credentials.py:74`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/containercluster_admin_credentials/tasks/update.yml:14`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/containercluster_admin_credentials.py:16`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/admin_credentials_protocol.py:8`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/admin_credential_run.go:48`,
`internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/invocation.go:255`

**Scenario:** An operator runs `bootwright cluster update-admin-credentials
--name \<c>` (the prepare operation behaves the same way). The kubeadmin
account may have been removed after an identity provider was configured, or
the API may be unreachable. The credential helper raises one of nine distinct
ValueErrors (module_utils/containercluster_admin_credentials.py:16-59). The
module catches all of them and calls one fixed fail_json
(containercluster_admin_credentials.py:73-74). The role task runs under no_log
with no failed_when, so the playbook stops there. The protocol only publishes
`loaded` and `completed`, so no `refused` record exists. The runner maps the
non-zero exit to the generic lifecycle.state failure. The Go diagnostic
access.unavailable (admin_credential_run.go:48-52) is reachable only when the
playbook finishes without proof, which the module never allows. The spec
promises these refusals.

**What the operator sees:** lifecycle.state: 'the adapter operation did not
complete'. The remedy tells the operator to read the adapter output kept
beside this attempt's log. That output holds only the censored notice, so the
pointer leads nowhere. Nothing names the cluster account, the cause, or
whether the password already changed.

**Impact:** The operator cannot tell a missing account (permanent, the command
will never succeed) from an API outage (repeat) or a half-applied update
(repeat to converge). The cause text exists only in a ValueError that is
thrown away. Medium: the spec promises specific refusals and none is shown.

**Recovery today:** Repeat the command and hope. Reading the retained adapter
output does not help, because it shows only the censored notice.

**Proposed fix (effort M):** Give the module a closed list of reasons
(account-unavailable, account-replaced, account-changed, update-unproved,
api-unavailable). Add a refused phase to the credentials protocol, run the
task with failed_when: false, and publish a refused record. In Go, map each
reason to a diagnostic that names the cluster and the remedy, as the install
does.

#### G02-02

**A Ceph package transaction cut part way refuses package-drift on every
repeat apply, and the message wrongly says 'completed' and names neither
destroy-then-apply nor dnf history undo**

Medium · dead end · apply · verified: combined narrowed, arbiter narrowed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/ceph_packages.py:300`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/native_apply.py:136`,
`internal/storage/ceph/host.go:487`, `specs/ceph.md:256`,
`internal/storage/ceph/requests.go:347`

**Scenario:** An apply runs a Ceph host's package block. native_apply.apply
runs the transaction (run4, native_apply.py:136). Part way through, the run is
cut by Ctrl-C, the run deadline or a reboot. Some packages are installed,
others are not. decision.json and verified.json persist and complete.json is
absent. On repeat apply, prepare() skips the completed branch. The installed
packages match neither the recorded after state nor the before state. The
require at ceph_packages.py:300 refuses package-drift, and a unit test pins
that no new plan is solved. Every repeat refuses the same way. The host
identity (FSIDFor, requests.go:347) comes from the apply operation, so only a
new apply gets a fresh decision.

**What the operator sees:** lifecycle.unknown 'the Ceph host's installed
packages no longer match its completed package decision', with remedy 'inspect
the host's installed packages against the retained package decision;
Bootwright never installs over a foreign inventory'. No completion was
recorded, so 'completed' is wrong. The decision is a root-owned journal on the
host. The remedy names no command.

**Impact:** Medium: wrong and missing remedy, and recovery by non-obvious
steps. An interrupted run is a realistic trigger. The operator is left
guessing which exit to take.

**Recovery today:** Destroy the context's apply, then apply again. A new apply
gets a fresh decision over the partial packages. This is inferred from
FSIDFor, not driven, and that destroy succeeds over a partly installed host is
unverified. Alternatively, repair the packages by hand with `dnf history undo`
back to the recorded before state.

**Proposed fix (effort M):** Keep the refusal, but give it its own reason and
wording when verified.json exists, complete.json is absent and the packages
match neither recorded state. Name the host and the exits: `dnf history undo`
to the recorded before state, or destroy and apply again. Drop the word
'completed' on this path.

**Already recorded:** Partly. B79 (specs/ceph.md:256-257 leaves 'interruption
qualification' to B79), but the drift wording and remedy are not tracked.

#### G02-03

**Container cluster media publication reports one fixed sentence, with no path
or cause, for I/O faults and other errors that are not a layout refusal**

Low · output · both · verified: combined confirmed, combined narrowed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/modules/containercluster_media_token.py:298-299`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/modules/containercluster_media_layout.py:82-84`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/containercluster_publication.py:60-66`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/containercluster_publication.py:99-100`

**What:** Two helper functions in the publication code (ancestor() and step())
re-raise a raw OSError. Both media modules catch it in a second branch and
fail with a fixed sentence. Only a LayoutError names a directory. The token
module's branch also catches ValueError and KeyError, and a missing published
source image. Realistic triggers are EIO, ENOSPC during publish (token module
only, because the layout module only reads), and a directory chain with more
than 40 symbolic links. EACCES is unlikely because the adapter runs as root.
Unclassified I/O faults therefore escape the refusal vocabulary that names the
directory to fix.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Wrap OSError in a LayoutError that carries the
current directory and a closed problem class (permission, space, link-limit,
io), so the existing refusal names the directory.

#### G02-05

**policy trade-off: removeCertificateAfterBoot deletes any slot holding the
authority, even one the operator installed earlier, while the spec says it
deletes the imported certificate**

Low · unsafe · both · verified: combined narrowed, combined narrowed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/redfish_remote_ca.py:144-146`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/redfish_remote_ca.py:153-157`,
`specs/api/machines.md:632`, `specs/substrates.md:2159-2183`,
`internal/substrate/target.go:353`

**What:** The Machine declares importCertificate and
removeCertificateAfterBoot. The organization CA that issues the artifact
server's certificate already sits in a FileTransfer slot, installed by the
operator for other uses. RemoteCA.apply() finds the match and returns
unchanged without recording that it did not import the slot. The eject then
removes any slot matching the authority fingerprint, so the operator's anchor
is deleted. redfish_control.py:825-846 and the certificate-collection path do
the same. The spec is ambiguous: machines.md:632 says the eject 'deletes the
imported certificate', while substrates.md says it removes 'a slot proved to
contain that authority' and that settling converges to the target rather than
undoing the attempt's own writes. The trigger is rare and opt-in.
removeCertificate comes from desired state, not custody.

**Proposed fix (effort M):** Record in the attempt's evidence whether insert
imported the slot or found it, and remove only a slot the insert imported. The
fix must still let an eject after an interrupted insert remove what that
insert left, so it is not a drop-in change.

**Ten disk-discovery ValueErrors are absent from REFUSALS and all report 'a
bounded discovery contract was refused'; about three are causes an operator
can hit**

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/disk_discovery_media.py:67`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/disk_discovery_media.py:135`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/disk_discovery_media.py:148`,

`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/disk_discovery_boot.py:110-137`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/disk_discovery_ssh.py:52`

**What:** diagnostic() looks up the error text in REFUSALS and falls back to
code 'contract', whose fixed text is 'a bounded discovery contract was
refused'. Ten literals are unmapped: image component size, initrd link cycle,
source image path, scratch cleanup, initramfs path, entry and overlay, image
payload, report size, and custody entry bound (ssh.py:52, added by a
verifier). An initrd over 256 MiB in the operator's source ISO raises

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Add the operator-reachable literals (component

#### G02-07

**A kill inside the short write window of the shared atomic_publish helper
leaves a hidden stage file that nothing reaps, in the directories of all five
callers**

Low · loose end · both · verified: combined narrowed, combined narrowed

**Where:**
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/atomic_publish.py:35-36`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/atomic_publish.py:47-52`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/libvirt_nm_carrier.py:151`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/libvirt_nm_carrier.py-218`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/libvirt_firewall_ready.py:219`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/libvirt_vlan_refusal.py:286`

**What:** atomic_publish creates a hidden stage file at line 36 (for the
NetworkManager carrier, '.bootwright-carrier-\<hex>'). It removes the stage in
a finally block, which cannot run on SIGKILL. If the adapter tree is killed or
power is lost between stage creation and os.replace, the stage stays. That
window covers the write, chmod and fsync, so it is milliseconds wide. Nothing
lists or reaps these names. The carrier's remove path unlinks only the final
name. Five callers share the helper, so the same stage can leak in each
caller's directory, not only /etc/NetworkManager/conf.d. The helper only
promises that a failed publication removes its stage and that after a crash
the name holds the old file or the whole new one.

**Proposed fix (effort S):** Fix it in the shared helper, for example by
reaping stale stages of its prefix on the next publish, or add a per-directory
reaper. Do not patch the carrier alone.

**The substrate dispatcher republishes only `<arm>_refusal`; the baremetal and

Low · loose end · both · verified: combined narrowed, combined narrowed

`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_machine/tasks/dispatch.yml:25`,
`ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_baremetal_machine/tasks/media_eject.yml:10`,

nothing reads it. The real refusal text travels in the port result message,
